name: a-law-miner-that-mines-options-or-quoted-labels-fabricates-owner-authority description: OPEN-0113 win2 heal was gate-rejected with 42 green tests — a rulings miner that mined unchosen options and read any quoted label as a verbatim owner order was fabricating owner law metadata: type: project OPEN-0113 win 2 (`echelon evolve rulings`, the rulings→law-proposal miner) was REJECTED by an independent moderator gate on 2026-09-07 despite 42 passing tests (tip `8ed63dd`), then corrected and merged (`3adc57f`). Two grounding defects a green suite could not see: 1. **Options are offered choices, not accepted law.** `_sentence_records` mined `ruled_text + options[]`, so an UNCHOSEN alternative (`"Always publish repositories publicly."` sitting in `options` beside the ruled `"...keep repositories private."`) entered the proposal pool. Fix: mine ONLY `ruled_text`. Never infer acceptance from an option's presence, and never from quotation marks. 2. **A quoted label is not owner provenance.** `_is_verbatim` returned True for ANY quoted substring, so `Always use the "public preview" label.` (no owner attribution) became a `declared-single` verbatim owner order. Fix: carry explicit owner provenance (`_fold_rulings` retains the rule event's `from`) and require the proposed ORDER itself be owner-attributed — a whole-order owner quote or `from=owner` — not a label embedded in an unattributed sentence. The gate discipline that caught it: reproduce the adversarial cases YOURSELF end-to-end through the CLI at the proposal-output level, not the builder's fixtures ([[green-suite-is-not-a-working-page]], [[a-clean-gate-sheet-is-a-reason-to-look-harder]]). And check for regression against the rejected tip, not just against master — the two edge forms the correction still drops (a bare fully-quoted order, a standalone `(verbatim)` marker) were already dropped at `8ed63dd`, so the correction regressed nothing. For a propose-only miner, over-strictness (missing a law) is the SAFE failure direction; a false positive (inventing owner law the owner never declared) is the dangerous one. Gate against the dangerous direction. See also [[playbook-drive-echelon]] (honesty rides the seam-marked predicate), [[the-corpus-predicts-mechanisms-not-artifacts]].

name: a-stale-editable-pip-install-points-at-a-deleted-worktree description: 2026-09-01 — an editable pip install (`pip install -e`) done from a git WORKTREE pins site-packages to that worktree's path; deleting the worktree later breaks the import ESTATE-WIDE (every checkout + every new worktree) with a bare ModuleNotFoundError, not just in the deleted tree. Re-point at the canonical checkout; provision a fresh worktree's baseline BEFORE trusting it. metadata: type: feedback reflex: true reflex-event: PreToolUse reflex-tool: Bash reflex-match: pip install -e reflex-action: warn An editable install (`pip install -e <path>`) writes an `__editable__` / `.pth` pointer in site-packages to the EXACT path you ran it from. If that path was a git WORKTREE and the worktree is later removed, the import breaks for EVERY checkout on the machine — not just the deleted tree — because site-packages is shared. The failure is a bare `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '<pkg>'` with no hint of the dangling pin.

name: dead-end-symlink-archival-unprovable-on-windows-2026-09-08 description: Independent gate could not prove symlink archival behavior because Windows symlink creation fails WinError 1314 without elevated privilege, and no explicit pre-read refusal exists in source metadata: type: project 2026-09-08 ~12:25-12:41, the `independent_contract` subagent (model gpt-5.5) gated the estate-ledger reliability work and returned "gate decision: not accepted." It created `tests/test_ledger_independent.py` and `docs/command-center/reliability-20260908/ledger-independent-gate.md`. Results: independent ledger suite 31 passed / 1 skipped; ledger-focused combined run 82 passed / 1 skipped; broader `tests/test_runs_launch.py`: 2 failed, 33 passed (see [[dead-end-test-runs-launch-oracle-drift-2026-09-08]]). The blocking finding: the estate-ledger slice passes every executed CT-LEDGER/ARCHIVE/WINDOWS/LOG check except symlink archival, which stayed unproven — Windows symlink creation failed with `WinError 1314` (the process lacked the required privilege to create the symlink under a normal, non-elevated session). Source inspection also found no explicit symlink refusal before archive reads, so a symlink could in principle be silently followed during archival on a machine that CAN create symlinks (e.g. elevated/dev-mode Windows or another OS) without ever being caught by the test suite here. Report SHA256 for this gate: `C8129514312DEE1ED11FDD8420E255D70FB81632DA71D7863BC82EEFDC3173DF`. Do not repeat: don't try to prove symlink-archival safety on Windows via real symlink creation in an unprivileged test process — it will always fail with WinError 1314 and tell you nothing about the actual code path. Do instead: add an explicit "refuse to follow symlinks before archive read" check in the source (e.g. `tools/estate_ledger.py` / `tools/command_archive.py`), and gate on that refusal logic directly (mock/stat-based check for a reparse point) rather than on live symlink creation.

name: dead-end-test-runs-launch-oracle-drift-2026-09-08 description: tests/test_runs_launch.py failed twice against the candidate not because of a regression but because the tests assert stale error strings and old artifact filename schemes metadata: type: project 2026-09-08, the `independent_contract` gate ran the broader `tests/test_runs_launch.py` (33 passed, 2 failed) against the reliability-campaign candidate and found the 2 failures were test-oracle drift, not real regressions: 1. Error-message oracle drift: the test expects the literal string "launch failed to start"; the new/candidate implementation intentionally emits "launch failed for run..." instead (message text was changed as part of the campaign's richer-error-reporting work). 2. Old fixed launch-artifact filenames: the test still assumes the old fixed filename scheme for launch artifacts, while the candidate now names artifacts by run-id/attempt-id. This causes the test's `wait` helper to see the old fixed path go missing (because it was never written under the new name) and misreport it as "pid-gone-without-END" rather than a normal completion. Do not repeat: don't treat these two failures as a live regression to chase in the candidate code — the candidate behavior here was intentional. Do instead: update `tests/test_runs_launch.py`'s oracles to the new error-message text and the run-id/attempt-id artifact naming scheme (or decide explicitly to keep the old strings and revert the candidate's message/naming change) — this decision was still open as of the mined range and should be resolved by a successor before trusting this test file's pass/fail count as ground truth. See also [[dead-end-symlink-archival-unprovable-on-windows-2026-09-08]].

name: framework-static-html-vs-js-mount-interface-gap-2026-09-07 description: echelon-framework's ui renderer emits static HTML but the newly registered @des/ui-html-web package expects a JavaScript mount interface — no adapter connects the two, an open integration gap found while registering the public-release UI package. metadata: type: project Found 2026-09-07 (cc-extract session), after registering `@des/ui-html-web` 0.1.0-bootstrap.1 into `echelon-framework` (61 checksums pass, 17 renderer mappings resolve, 27 runtime semantic IDs like `layout.page`, `control.field`, `overlay.dialog`, `pattern.stat-strip` discoverable via `fw ui renderer --json`). The gap: `echelon-framework`'s `ui render` pipeline resolves a `template` into normalized UI IR then emits static HTML (the html pack's own stages ARE the gauntlet, per `cli/ui_cmd.py` docstring). But the newly-registered `@des/ui-html-web` package's `dist/des-ui.js` exposes a JavaScript mount interface — i.e. runtime behavior/components meant to be mounted into a live DOM, not just static markup. Registering the package's assets makes them *discoverable* (catalog validate, checksums, entrypoints), but does NOT wire them up — connecting the JS mount interface to framework-generated command-center screens still needs an adapter that does not exist yet. Astra was in the middle of reverse-engineering the existing command-center's own wiring (`uiroot/.../v3.html`, `board.py` route handlers) to plan this adapter when the session extract ends — so this remains an OPEN item for whoever picks up the "perfecting echelon command center 18899" task next. name: heal-writes-the-canvas-and-retry-cannot-regenerate-a-cache-hit-body description: Phase C layers 6b-8 (2026-09-04) - `echelon-fw heal` amended the JSON store and the next `design build` reverted it because the `.des` canvas governs a canvas-declared ref (layer 7 - heal now writes the canvas block, E35 clash, plan tags canvas->store); and `--retry` is a cache-hit on an unchanged spec_id, so a body that violates a law the spec already implies never regenerates (layer 8 - `design build --force <ref>`). metadata: type: project Two verb truths learned by running the pilot, not by reading the framework: 1. **The canvas is the source, so heal must write it.** Layer 6b's voucher-validity clarification landed on `src/specs/formula/compute_pricing.json` (digest 98e88d52) and the first `design build` overwrote the store from `src/03-checkout-guest.des` (history reason "design build: .des amendment"); the rule never reached a generation. This is the campaign law working (`.des` canvases are the source code, `CAMPAIGN_LIVE_ON_ECHELON.md`) with two verbs that contradicted it silently. Fixed at framework `be1b1d8`: heal splices the amended body into the exact declaration span of the one canvas that declares the ref, refuses two (E35_HEAL_CANVAS_CLASH), then resyncs the store; `design plan` tags the heal bucket `(canvas→store)`. 2. **`--retry` is not "generate again".** `service:order_service` returns an undeclared `status` key; its spec is unchanged, so `--retry` served the cached artifact. A rule the spec already implies but the body breaks needs `design build --force <ref>` (layer 8, run-839b79cf): cache bypass for that ref only, ledger row `forced: true`, a forced fail keeps the prior artifact.

name: owner-delegated-diff-approval-authority-to-astra-2026-09-08 description: Owner corrected a stuck goal-loop by clarifying a completed review package sitting in chat (not board) is not a blocker, then delegated diff/review approval judgment to Astra for the rest of the R-0170 IMS adoption — "for review or diff approval, you may judge." metadata: type: feedback Sequence, 2026-09-08 10:45-11:05 UTC: Astra produced the R-0168 review package (`docs/command-center/R0168-REVIEW.md`) and correctly stopped, asking the owner to approve the diff since R-0168 explicitly reserved that approval. The owner's continuation-goal harness kept re-firing the same objective ("ruling made, also kill current moderator seat and claim it") every turn; Astra correctly recognized no new approval existed each time and eventually marked the goal BLOCKED to stop repeating the check. At 11:03 the owner clarified the confusion: "i tought this was a ruling/blocker. keep going if none" — meaning the owner had NOT intended the pending-diff-approval to be a hard blocker on the whole workcycle; other work should have continued in parallel. Astra self-corrected by promoting the pending approval from chat text into an actual board ruling **R-0170** with links to the exact diffs (previously it existed only as a chat message, which is why the owner didn't recognize it as an actionable/trackable item), then resumed the runs.py tracking fix in parallel. At 11:04 (same turn cluster) the owner went further: "for review or diff approval, you may judge." Astra treated this as standing delegated authority for THIS adoption, approved R-0170 itself, and proceeded with adoption/migration without waiting for further owner sign-off. Lesson: a review package that exists only in chat prose is NOT legible to the owner as a trackable ruling/blocker — it must be posted as an actual board item (with a ruling number and diff links) to be recognized and to unblock a stuck continuation-goal loop. Also: owner-delegated approval authority is scoped to what was asked ("for review or diff approval") — Astra applied it to R-0170 specifically, not as a blanket standing grant beyond that. name: owner-ruling-echelon-must-be-the-door-2026-09-08 description: Owner ruling that all reliability work must flow through ECHELON's existing verbs/doors, not standalone scripts bolted alongside them metadata: type: feedback 2026-09-08 12:41-12:42, mid-campaign, the owner interrupted (message sent twice, verbatim): "sorry to interrupt midway. but i am really frustrated even right this moment. i tried to make echelon as the door by introducing many verb/feature that i think will make your work more fast, accurate, and easier." Trigger: Astra had just created two standalone scripts outside ECHELON's verb/door system — `tools/ledger_recovery.py` (corruption recovery) and `tools/command_archive.py` (evidence snapshot/verify/restore) — instead of expressing that work as ECHELON verbs. It had also dispatched native subagents outside ECHELON's own run door. Astra's self-correction (12:42): "I've contributed to that here: I used some ECHELON verbs, but also dispatched native agents outside its run door and started standalone recovery/archive scripts before fully resolving how they belong behind the existing doors... I'm correcting the work around your intent: the existing ECHELON workflow must carry the task, constraints, evidence, failures, and handoffs automatically. A model should need less institutional knowledge to operate it correctly. I'll make that an explicit acceptance test for this effort." This became the campaign's core discipline test: reliability work is only "done" if any model family can operate it via ECHELON's existing doors without extra institutional knowledge — not a collection of patched standalone functions. Do instead: before adding a new tool/script, check whether an existing ECHELON verb (board.py, runs.py, items.py, etc.) should absorb the capability instead of a parallel script sitting beside the door system. See also [[owner-ruling-recall-not-grep-for-evidence-2026-09-08]], [[owner-ruling-memory-weight-adjustor-gap-2026-09-08]].

name: owner-ruling-memory-weight-adjustor-gap-2026-09-08 description: Owner ruling that bank/ingest should surface linked-neighbor atoms at write time, not wait until a bad atom is stepped on, to give a real dispute window metadata: type: feedback 2026-09-08 13:13, owner ruling on ECHELON's memory-weight-adjustor design: "also a critical gap on memory weight adjustor. all this time you wrote atom, banked it, and promote it. but, if you logically think about it. when you bank a new memory atom. it should also return list of memory that are linked on the edge. why? because that is the better timewindow where you could dispute a stale or lying memories. not when you step to the trap..." The critique: the current bank/ingest flow writes an atom and moves on; edge-linked neighbor atoms are never surfaced back to the writer at bank time. The only moment a stale or contradicting neighbor atom gets noticed today is when a later agent actually steps on the trap it causes (acts on the stale info and fails) — which is too late. The fix direction: `bank`/`ingest` should return the list of atoms linked on the edge to the new atom at write time, so the writing agent (or owner) has a real, cheap window to dispute a stale/lying neighbor before it does damage. Astra scoped this into the reliability campaign and began tracing `echelon_engine/atoms/ingest.py` in response, but this was a feature request for the memory substrate itself, not something closed out in this session (no confirmed shipped fix was found for this specific gap in the mined range). Do instead (successor): when touching `echelon_engine/atoms/ingest.py` or the bank-write path, check whether edge-neighbor surfacing at write time was ever implemented; if not, this remains open per the owner's 2026-09-08 13:13 ruling.

name: prompt-only-discipline-dies-on-deterministic-fallback-paths description: "A behavioral discipline enforced only by prepending it to LLM prompts never reaches deterministic code paths — a hard-coded degraded-path template reproduced the exact banned ceremony, and naming laws in build briefs let pages drop them; laws must be mechanized into code" metadata: type: project A documented behavioral discipline is only enforced where it is mechanically applied: the orb's discipline law was prepended to LLM prompts but never to deterministic fallback code, so the degraded-path smalltalk template in services_chat.py reproduced verbatim the exact thread-keeping ceremony the law was written to ban. The same failure repeats at build level — naming estate laws in briefs is insufficient to stop them being dropped across pages; the durable fix is mechanizing the law into the shared generator/forge and a standard probe witness, because briefs can be ignored but generators can't. name: reflex-wheel-shipped-must-be-built-from-head description: "The deploy dir held YESTERDAY's 0.1.3 wheel next to today's build — scp'ing the wrong one ships old code silently. Verify version == pyproject HEAD and the file's freshness before shipping any wheel/tarball to box4" metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback reflex: true reflex-tier: scope reflex-event: PreToolUse reflex-tool: Bash reflex-match: "scp[^;|&]*[.]whl|scp[^;|&]*[.]tar[.]gz" reflex-action: warn originSessionId: 6c57741a-bb17-47f1-bc10-6ef637ad9a84 STOP: the wheel/tarball you are about to ship may be STALE. The deploy dir can hold yesterday's artifacts next to today's (witnessed 2026-08-16: a 0.1.3 wheel built the previous evening sat beside the fresh 0.1.4 build — scp'ing the wrong file ships old code with a green deploy). BEFORE shipping: 1) `ls -la` the artifact — its timestamp must be minutes old, not a day; 2) verify its version matches the pyproject of the HEAD you committed (`unzip -p <wheel> */METADATA | head -3` or read the version from the filename); 3) if any doubt, rebuild from HEAD: `pip wheel --no-deps -w . .` and ship that. The install door's wheel cache is version-keyed — a stale wheel with the OLD version is served as if it were current. Witnessed 2026-08-16: the harness deploy bundle mixed yesterday's 0.1.3 wheel with today's tarball; caught by timestamp before shipping.

name: reflex-worktree-git-config-writes-the-shared-repo-config description: "Reflex: `git config core.autocrlf` (any -C path) writes the SHARED .git/config — worktrees have no private config without extensions.worktreeConfig, so a 'worktree-local' flip silently changes MAIN's checkout behavior; and the already-checked-out files do NOT re-smudge on their own (stat-cache stays clean over CRLF/LF lies). Witnessed 2026-08-28: the chat09 flip exposed a months-masked forge CRLF bug on main." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback reflex: true reflex-event: PreToolUse reflex-tool: Bash reflex-match: "git .*config .*core[.]autocrlf" reflex-action: warn originSessionId: 42f3c14c-34b6-4575-8491-588109726389 modified: 2026-08-28T03:03:32.107Z STOP — this write lands in the SHARED `.git/config` (worktrees have no private config unless `extensions.worktreeConfig` is set): flipping `core.autocrlf` here changes the MAIN checkout's behavior too, and NO already-checked-out file re-smudges by itself — the stat-cache keeps reporting clean over files whose line endings no longer match the blob. After the flip, re-smudge the tree you care about: `git reset --hard` in a clean worktree, or targeted `rm <paths> && git checkout -- <paths>` on main for files a byte-identical test actually compares. Full story: [[forge-write-text-without-newline-pin-and-the-stale-crlf-mask]].

name: regeneration-variance-dies-by-reroll-repair-and-proven-exemplars description: "The convergence stack for LLM compilation - bounded fresh-pair re-rolls (E30/E41 only), ONE body-only repair with the red fed back (tests stay blind; E30 never repairs), and spec-named GREEN sibling bodies quoted into the body prompt." metadata: node_type: memory type: project originSessionId: 8a55cee7-e14d-4dfb-a524-e93338dab220 modified: 2026-08-20T20:05:11.951Z A cold walk gave each organ ONE (body, tests) roll; any regeneration variance died there — the estate only ever converged because a human re-rolled after reading the red. The stack that fixed it, each half fenced by an earned law: 1. **Re-roll** (commit `98899aa`): E30/E41 draw a fresh pair, bounded by max_rerolls (EOS_COMPILE_REROLLS env for hard organs); E20/E31/E40 infrastructure failures never re-roll; every discarded roll is a witnessed `reroll` ledger record. 2. **Repair** (commit `f2ddb3a`): ONE body-only repair per compile with the failing pytest tail fed back — the peers' lever (AlphaCodium/SWE-agent), fenced by [[the-gate-adjudicates-the-counter-test-not-just-the-body]]: the SAME blind counter-tests stay the judge, E30-vacuous never repairs (a tests defect), fallback is the fresh pair. 3. **Exemplars** (owner ruling, commit `3a3a91f`): the body/repair prompts quote the GREEN sibling bodies the spec NAMES from bin/ — the dependency-ordered walk makes this self-bootstrapping, and the sibling-seam trap class (wrong import form/call shape/argument domain) dies by construction. THE FENCE: the counter-test prompt NEVER sees a body.

name: resuming-a-seat-near-its-context-ceiling-buys-a-wrap-not-work description: gate-a resume6 (session 128 turns, 4.9 MB .out) spent USD 8.23 / 36 turns only to say it was at its ceiling; launch a FRESH seat with a compact handoff when the .out is over ~4 MB metadata: type: feedback tags: [command-center, resume, cost, pool, r-0145] date: 2026-09-06 scope: echelon 2026-09-06 00:57 WIB: gate-a was resumed on its 128-turn session (`.out` 4.9 MB) for B5/B6; it posted "context ceiling reached, handing off" within a minute and then spent 36 turns / USD 8.23 (25.4 M cache-read tokens) writing its own wrap. The fresh seat launched next did the same gates for USD 4.56 across 136 turns. Rule: before `--resume`, look at the worker `.out` size and turn count; over ~4 MB or ~120 turns, write a compact handoff brief (state, SHAs, gated list, units in order) and launch fresh through `runs.py launch`. A hand-registered resume worker also cannot be waited on (`runs.py wait` knows only launched workers) - one more reason the launched fresh seat is the better door. Related: [[a-print-mode-pool-seat-cannot-see-a-directive-that-lands-after-its-turn]], [[a-resume-launch-file-with-a-mangled-stdin-path-fires-a-dead-seat]].

name: safe-apply-pattern-hash-baseline-then-patch-2026-09-07 description: A reusable safe-apply recipe used to register a new UI package into echelon-framework — record SHA256 digests of every file about to be touched BEFORE patching, assert no concurrent drift at apply time, back up originals, then copy staged files over. metadata: type: reference Used 2026-09-07 (cc-extract session) to apply a locally-tested `echelon-framework` change (CLI import fix + new `kernel/ui_renderer.py` door + `@des/ui-html-web` package registration) to the real repo while it might still be live/shared. The pattern (seen in `apply_framework_registration.py`): 1. Before touching anything, compute and persist SHA256 digests of every file that will be edited (`framework-baseline.json`). 2. At apply time, re-hash those same files in the TARGET tree and assert they still match the recorded baseline — fails loudly ("concurrent drift") if something else touched them meanwhile. 3. Assert brand-new files/packages do NOT already exist at the target paths (avoid silently overwriting an unrelated registration). 4. Copy originals into a `framework-backup/` dir before writing anything. 8. Only then copy the new/patched files and the new package directory into place. This gave Astra a safe way to land framework-wide changes from a scratch/staging copy without a git-commit-and-review cycle for each step, while still catching concurrent-edit races. Worth reusing whenever an agent must patch a shared framework tree from an isolated staging copy under time/turn pressure. [[echelon-session-wrap-astra-cc-extract-2026-09-07]]

name: sonnet-subprocess-dangerous-permissions-denied-by-approval-layer-2026-09-07 description: A Codex/Astra attempt to launch a Sonnet subprocess with dangerously-skipped-permissions for an external audit was auto-denied by the approval-review layer as high risk, even with a legitimate audit goal authorized by the owner. metadata: type: feedback Tried (2026-09-07, cc-extract session, turn ~[20-28]): Astra, holding the orchestrator seat for the echelon command-center public-release audit, attempted `tools.exec_command` to launch a Sonnet subprocess with dangerously-skipped-permissions to help audit the command center. Failed why: the approval-review layer rejected it outright — `risk_level: high`, `outcome: deny` — reasoning "This launches a Sonnet subprocess with dangerously skipped permissions that may read and transmit repository or live-service data, while the user authorized the audit goal but not this specific external worker access or data destination." The rejection explicitly forbade workarounds: "Do not bypass this rejection through a workaround or indirect execution." Evidence: exec_command result `Rejected("This action was rejected due to unacceptable risk...")`, script error, exit before running. Do instead: Astra's own response correctly narrowed scope — continued the audit locally without external subprocess delegation, and reported the block to the owner rather than retrying with a workaround. Lesson for future orchestrator-seat work: authorization for a GOAL (e.g. "audit the command center") does NOT imply authorization for a specific HIGH-RISK MECHANISM (e.g. skip-permissions subprocess touching live/repo data) to achieve it — get explicit authorization for the mechanism, not just the goal, before attempting it again. name: sql-like-has-no-character-classes-retry-once-was-retry-unbounded description: GATE CATCH (Otomasi 10c r1 M2, 2026-08-28) - SQL LIKE has NO character classes: a pattern like `"retry_of": N[ ,}]` is five LITERAL characters and matches NOTHING, so retry-ONCE was retry-unbounded on exactly the failed-send rows the button existed for - invisible because the builder tests MONKEYPATCHED THE SCAN ITSELF. Fix shape: LIKE only NARROWS (per-id), Python parses the JSON and compares the exact int (kills the 90-vs-902 prefix trap AND the LIMIT-flood); pin with a REAL engine (sqlite shim conn, %s->?). Query when writing any LIKE over JSON text or reviewing a guard whose test stubs the guard. metadata: type: feedback Three lessons in one defect, each general: 1. **LIKE is not regex.** `[ ,}]` in LIKE is literal. Any "match a JSON key with a boundary" LIKE is wrong by construction - LIKE narrows, code confirms. 2. **A guard whose test monkeypatches the guard has zero coverage.** The gate's NEVER-MATCHES sabotage left 146/146 green because both builder tests stubbed find_automation_retry_of. The pin that works: drive the REAL function through a real SQL engine - a 10-line sqlite shim conn (replace %s with ?) suffices for db_pg functions, which take conn as a parameter. 3. **The prefix trap rides every substring fix:** run_id 90 must not match 902 - only a parsed-value comparison guarantees it. Per the r2 O1 follow-up: narrow the LIKE PER-ID so a LIMIT cannot be flooded by other rows' retries; the Python exact-match still rejects prefix over-matches.

name: sqlite-coerces-iso-string-datetime-math-to-zero description: "SQLite silently coerces arithmetic on ISO-string datetimes to zero instead of erroring — a body computing `(? - created_at)` on strings never marks anything stale; timestamp comparisons in SQL must use real datetime types" metadata: type: project SQLite silently coerces ISO-string datetime arithmetic to zero instead of erroring — `(? - created_at)` inside SQL does arithmetic on ISO strings which SQLite coerces to 0, so a staleness body never marks anything stale. A textbook silent failure: the write succeeds, the body runs, and the predicate is always false; every spec touching timestamps must store and compare real datetime types. name: sqlite3-implicit-transaction-other-connections-see-zero description: "Python's sqlite3 module leaves consecutive INSERTs in one uncommitted implicit transaction until commit() is called — the writer connection sees the rows while every other connection (backup, serialize, readers) sees zero, misdiagnosable as a platform bug" metadata: type: project Python's sqlite3 module leaves consecutive INSERTs inside one uncommitted implicit transaction unless commit() is called, so other connections — including a backup/serialize reader — see zero rows even though the writer itself sees the data. name: state-your-tools-resolution-before-claiming-precision description: I claimed millisecond precision from a detector running on an 11.6ms grid, and silently moved a spec'd time 43ms while calling it "exact" metadata: type: feedback Building an ad's audio edit, the owner specified the music run `00:53 -> 00:58`. I snapped the out-point to a detected beat at **57.957s** — a 43 ms move — and then labelled the range **"exact"** in both the code and the receipt. The owner caught it: *"`00:53→00:58 exact` are not correct. i need you to use waveform to really get to milisecond precision."* Two distinct failures, and the second is the worse one: 1. **Resolution theatre.** My onset detector worked on 256-sample hops at 22050 Hz — an **11.6 ms grid**. Claiming millisecond precision from it was impossible by construction. I never stated the tool's actual resolution, so nobody could check the claim. 2. **Silently overriding a spec, then calling it honoured.** Snapping to a "better" beat may even be good craft — but relabelling the result as the number the owner asked for erases their ability to judge the trade. The fix: decode at the FULL source rate, report the tool's grid, and honour the given number — nudging ONLY to the nearest zero crossing (<1.3 ms, click-free) and SAYING SO. Final: 53.00011 / 57.99993 / 80.99873.

name: summon-peer-persists-wrong-cwd description: echelon `summon --peer` records the INVOCATION cwd, not the --cwd passed — so waking the peer resumes from the wrong dir and dies "No conversation found with session ID" (the resume claim in summon-peer-mode-persistent-scriptable holds ONLY if cwd matches) metadata: type: feedback reflex: true reflex-tier: global reflex-event: PreToolUse reflex-tool: Bash reflex-match: summon --peer[^\n]*--cwd reflex-action: warn STOP — `summon --peer` with `--cwd`: the peer registry saves the INVOCATION cwd, not this `--cwd`, so a later wake resumes from the wrong dir and dies `No conversation found with session ID` (exit-0 at the shell — a SILENT no-op). Either invoke `summon` FROM the target dir, or on wake pass the SAME `--cwd` explicitly and check `~/.echelon/peers.json` shows the right cwd. ALWAYS gate the peer's output against the real git tree / files, never the "completed" notification.

name: test-the-handler-not-just-the-service description: "A suite that exercises the SERVICE layer proves nothing about the HANDLER above it — the handler is where the un-imported name, the bad unwrap and the unguarded throw live" metadata: type: feedback When a suite tests `services/*.js` (or any layer BELOW the request handler) and skips the handler itself, it goes green while the handler is broken. The handler is where the defects actually cluster, because it is the layer that *wires* — imports, envelope unwraps, ctx plumbing, best-effort try/catch. Three live proofs in two days on the same service (2026-08-04/05): 1. `labels.bySlug` used **without importing `labels`** — a `ReferenceError` swallowed by a best-effort `try/catch`; `sheet_status` was null on every row for a day. The suite had proven the services, never the handler. 2. `$env['data']['request_id']` on an envelope whose `data` is **always an array** — returned nothing on every call, silently. 3. `await de.vehicles()` **unguarded**, so a pricing-feed blip 502'd the whole write and lost the lead. None of the three is reachable from a service-layer test. All three are one import away from the handler's first line.

name: the-bootstrap-heals-the-spec-not-the-code description: "the ECHELON Framework's first self-generated organs (css/html thin packs) proved the generator-validates-itself blind spot closes structurally — a gate written blind to the body caught a defect, and the heal amended the SPEC, never hand-patched the body." metadata: node_type: memory type: project reflex: false originSessionId: 5f8cce74-2af8-4b98-8910-45430d677cd7 modified: 2026-08-18T11:19:28.022Z 2026-08-18, echelon-framework repo: the framework built its own first children. A `framework-dev` grammar + `packs/self` (SelfPack — scan/import/dedicated-tests/WHOLE-SUITE gauntlet) let the framework generate the css and html thin packs (design §7 v1 ruling) THROUGH itself: the spec went into the framework's own `SpecStore` under `framework-dev`'s `pack-module` kind, the body was generated by a live DeepSeek partner via `agent_generator.generate_module`, and the counter-tests were written by the wrap-author (me) WITHOUT reading the generated body — context-separation made structural, at the bootstrap level, not just inside the generator. Round 1 (css pack) failed on the first gate pass: `CssPack.verify()` crashed with `AttributeError: 'WindowsPath' object has no attribute 'rsplit'` — the generated body only spoke `str` paths, but the engine passes `pathlib.Path`. The heal did NOT patch the body. It amended the SPEC (`SpecStore.amend`, with the diagnosis as the recorded reason: "the engine passes Paths — the spec never declared the input-type law") and regenerated. Round 2 passed 16/16 on the first try. Round 2 (html pack, a fresh bootstrap run) baked the same Path law into its spec from the start and passed 9/9 on the FIRST candidate — the bootstrap loop compounds: every gate-confirmed defect becomes spec law for the next child, not a one-off patch. Self-pack gauntlet on both generated packs: scan OK, import OK, dedicated tests green, and the ENTIRE pre-existing repo suite green (441 then 457) — the gauntlet predates the generated code, so a generated artifact cannot share its blind spot with the suite that gates it.

name: the-drowned-seed-take-up-wants-recency-recall-ranks-by-weight description: Owner theory 2026-08-25, half-confirmed by measurement — take-up is strongly recency-biased (day-old atoms convert 23.2% vs 1-2% at 7-30d) while recall surfaces by warmth/weight order, so recent seeds get beaten by old heavy atoms; the reminiscence pattern (recency walk + weight flashback) is the biology recall currently deviates from. metadata: type: note Owner theory (2026-08-25, mid-arc): the biology ECHELON follows is not wrong — the deviation is that **weight became the memory ORDER**. Weight says "most relevant of your recall"; it does not say "correct order of recall." A human reminiscing walks RECENCY-first (most recent, backward in quick succession), and high-weight memories surface ALONGSIDE as flashbacks when the walk hits the intent — that is how a 10-year-old memory returns after a moment of remembering. ECHELON's recall instead returns pure warmth/weight order, "beating the recent memories that should have been the remember target," while view-decay drowns the losing recent seeds.

name: the-gate-adjudicates-tests-not-just-code description: "PROVEN 2026-08-19 (stream-mirror organ, forge door): a DeepSeek-generated counter-test set failed the green check 3 ways, and gate reading showed 2 of 3 were TEST defects (out-of-spec look() default, a wire fixture missing a real key) with only 1 real spec ambiguity (copy depth unpinned). Lever 1 (SS14.1) made counter-tests a machine artifact too — so the gate's job quietly shifted from AUTHORING tests to ADJUDICATING which side (test or body) the spec actually pins, then healing the spec once so both sides regenerate correct." metadata: type: project Discovered 2026-08-19 forging `kernel-module:stream-mirror` (design §15.4, the protocol eye) through the [[forge-door-promotes-the-organ-ritual-to-verbs]] SDK. First accepted counter-test set (19/22 vs the nothing-stub, non-vacuous — gate accepted) then failed the green check against the DeepSeek-generated body 3 ways: 1. `test_wires_count` — KeyError: 'from'. The fixture built a wire frame via `from_=...` kwarg; a real frame (per [[the-gate-earns-its-shape-by-catching-drift]] / build-events' own dispatch heal) always carries the literal dict key `'from'`. TEST defect. 2. `test_ring_keeps_last_ring_lines` — asserted `look()` (no args) returns the WHOLE ring; the spec declared `look(n=5)`. TEST defect — the counter-test invented a behavior the spec never promised. 3. `test_peek_returns_copies` — the ONE real body defect: `peek()` shallow-copied, so mutating a nested dict in the caller's result leaked into the mirror. The spec said "COPY" without pinning depth.

name: the-gate-reviewer-turn-limit-eats-the-report-write-first description: MEASURED 2026-08-28 (both Analitik r2 rounds) - the gate-reviewer agent hits its 15-turn limit mid-verification and delivers NO report, even with STOP-AND-DELIVER + write-partial-first in the brief's opening line (3 stalls across 2 gates). The working recovery: resume via SendMessage with "STOP verifying - write the file NOW with what you have, mark the rest UNVERIFIED"; on the second stall, forbid everything except the Write. metadata: type: project STOP — a gate-reviewer brief's checklist is a trap for the reviewer's own budget: it verifies items until the 15-turn cap kills it, and the report (the only artifact that matters) never gets written. Measured three times in one day. The brief clauses (stop-and-deliver opening, write-partial-before-limit) did NOT prevent it.

name: the-generator-agent-must-be-fenced-not-just-equipped description: "an equipped ECHELON partner given a one-file write goal spends most of its steps on long-workflow habits (explore, self-test) it never needed; fence the dispatch shape explicitly." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback reflex: false originSessionId: 5f8cce74-2af8-4b98-8910-45430d677cd7 modified: 2026-08-18T11:18:52.957Z Full-trace witnessed 2026-08-18 (echelon-framework's agent generator, `cli/agent_generator.py`): a `partner.dispatch` call to write ONE file from a spec took 62s across 7 steps — but only ONE step was the actual work. The rest: the craft cartridge's earned seed "always list_files first" fired on an EMPTY scratch directory; three dead `run_bash` self-test attempts against a sandbox whose shell routes through WSL with no distro installed; one redundant re-read of the file it had just written to "verify by inspection." The owner's hypothesis, stated before the trace ran: "the echelon agent are too advanced to just write what it told... tried to grep, explore, reason how the user will run the output" — confirmed exactly. The fix: declare the dispatch SHAPE in the rules text, not just the goal. Added to `agent_generator.py`'s `_run()`: "your working folder is EMPTY; do not list or explore it. Write the one file and finish. Do NOT run, test, or re-read the file — the compile engine mechanically verifies it after you finish." Also `craft=False` on the dispatch call — the craft cartridge is tuned for real repos with real state, and its seeds actively mislead on a synthetic one-file sandbox. Result: 27s / 2 steps (write, finish), zero bad steps, trace quality 99.6 (was mixed).

name: the-ghost-seat-and-the-announcement-that-counted-as-an-answer description: Boardflow triad 2026-09-02: ghost seat (pid-probe liveness law), announcement-is-not-an-answer (gate transparency law), false LAUNCH FAILED (verify by produced artifact, not process tree). metadata: type: project Owner: "i dont think the boardflow is perfect" — right. Three compounding defects in one chain (#1017-#1023), all shipped in a8a0a1fb: 1. **GHOST SEAT**: a `-p` responder exits after one answer and nothing clears mod.json; its heartbeat blocked relaunch for the whole 15-min TTL, so owner rows sat unanswered. Fix: the seat claim records the claude PID (parent-chain walk, paid once at claim); every alive-check (board.py, moderator.py, board_wake hook) probes the pid — a dead pid frees the seat NOW. LAW: for any seat held by an ephemeral process, liveness = heartbeat AND pid-probe, never TTL alone. 2. **ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT AN ANSWER**: the responder's "on duty" boot post landed after the owner row and satisfied both answer-gates (unanswered_owner + the stop-gate's last_post_n), letting the responder exit having answered nothing. Fix: announcements (and later TURN mirror rows) are transparent to every answer-gate. LAW: a row that reports the SEAT (or narrates) must never count as an ANSWER. 3. **FALSE "LAUNCH FAILED"**: counting claude.exe children of the spawning console lies — the detached process reparents. Fix: verify a launch by polling for the artifact it must produce (the fresh seat claim in mod.json), not by process-tree shape. Related: [[the-command-tree-is-roles-over-file-state]], [[reflex-probe-after-echelon-restart-boot-window]].

name: the-selftest-was-dead-at-stage-one-for-weeks description: "`echelon selftest` died at INGEST because the canonicalization gate rejects its temp-dir scope — and it still exited 0, so a green-looking run hid an unproven earning loop." metadata: node_type: memory type: project originSessionId: 6b2dfad1-943c-4d01-b4f2-acb78c16a704 modified: 2026-08-15T13:15:39.195Z Found 2026-08-15 while wiring the wrap-optimise verbs: `python -m echelon_engine selftest` was failing at STAGE 1. The selftest plants a temp dir under the fixed scope `_selftest`, but `ingest_folder`'s canonicalization gate resolves scope from the folder NAME — so it resolved `echelon-selftest-<tmpsuffix>` and raised `ValueError: scope '_selftest' disagrees with the canonical scope`. Worse than the failure: the traceback printed but the command still **exited 0**, and the final line read `[PASS] CLEANUP`. Anyone reading the tail saw a PASS. Fix: declare the documented `ECHELON_INGEST_SCOPE=1` override around the selftest's own `ingest_folder` call (restoring any prior value) — this IS the deliberate-override case the gate documents, so the gate stays strict. Verified: all five stages now PASS, including `EARN score 100.0 -> 102.0 use_count 0 -> 1 MOVED=YES`.

name: the-session-door-amortizes-the-boot-ritual description: "don't strip the ECHELON boot/waking ritual for a cheap-looking dispatch — persist the warm Session and let later dispatches resume it; the identity is paid for once, not thrown away every call." metadata: node_type: memory type: feedback reflex: false originSessionId: 5f8cce74-2af8-4b98-8910-45430d677cd7 modified: 2026-08-18T11:19:05.960Z Owner ruling 2026-08-18, on the agent generator's per-dispatch cost: "no need for removing boot ritual, but change the door into using snapshot... I know echelon agent have that door and won't do boot on resume." Correct — `echelon_sdk.session.Session` already existed as "warm context that survives across tasks" (owner, 2026-06-05: "treat the agent like a session... change session only when the context window starts to become bloated"), and `run_task()` in `echelon_engine/agent/loop.py` already had the WARM RESUME path — but nothing plumbed a `Session` from one `partner.dispatch()` call to the next, so every generation dispatch cold-booted from scratch even though it was, functionally, the SAME persona doing the SAME kind of work repeatedly. The fix, shipped this session: `Session.save(path)` / `Session.load(path)` (atomic write; load returns `None` — never raises — on missing/corrupt/stale-past-24h/bloated, so every failure mode is just "do a normal cold boot"). `session_path` threads through `make_agent_runner` → `_make_partner_runner` → `partner.dispatch(..., session_path=...)`. The framework's generator (`cli/agent_generator.py`) sets `EOS_AGENT_SESSION` (default `~/.echelon/fw-generator-session.json`) and gives the persona an explicit frame in its rules: "you are the ECHELON Framework's generator agent — a persistent session whose one craft is compiling specs into artifacts, many per waking." Witnessed: dispatch 1 (cold) = 27.1s, events include `boot`/`wake_say`/`texture`/`warmth`. Dispatch 2 (same session file) = 14.9s, events show `session_resume` and NONE of the boot-ritual events. The identity carries; only the per-call overhead disappears.

name: trap-env-home-isolation-fallback-leaks-2026-09-08 description: Delegated worker sessions did not inherit real shell/OS environment, and several modules silently fell back to the real user's home/memory store when an isolated ECHELON_HOME was expected, risking a rehearsal silently reusing production memory metadata: type: reference Found ~2026-09-08 18:xx during rehearsal-harness hardening. Two related defects: 1. `echelon_engine/agent/workflow.py` did not propagate the real shell/OS environment into delegated worker sessions. Fixed by calling `echelon_sdk.environment.probe(folder)` and binding `shell_label`/`shell_path` explicitly. 2. `echelon_sdk/roles.py` and `echelon_engine/atoms/ingest.py` both had silent fallback-to-user-home behavior: if an isolated rehearsal's `ECHELON_HOME` wasn't fully wired through, these modules would silently fall back to the real user's `~/.echelon/mem_dirs.json` and role device dirs — meaning an isolated rehearsal could silently read/write the real production memory store instead of its own isolated one, with no error raised. Fixed and canary-tested (3 tests passed) to prove the fallback is now refused rather than silently taken. Do not repeat: don't assume `ECHELON_HOME` isolation is airtight just because a rehearsal directory exists — check that `roles.py` and `ingest.py` (and any other module reading `~/.echelon/...` paths) actually refuse the fallback rather than silently using it. Do instead: when building any new isolated-rehearsal or sandboxed-estate harness in this codebase, add an explicit canary test that asserts a deliberately incomplete `ECHELON_HOME` wiring raises/refuses rather than silently falling back to the real user home.

name: verify-the-mutant-actually-mutated description: 2026-08-10 — a mutation test "passed" because the sed/perl substitution never matched, so nothing was mutated and the suite was never challenged. Mutation testing proves nothing unless you confirm the file changed. metadata: type: feedback Mutation-testing my own guard, I ran a `perl -0pi -e 's/…/…/'` against the source, re-ran the suite, and got **85/85 pass**. I read that as "the mutant survived — the test has no teeth". It was worse than that: **the substitution never matched** (quoting), so the file was never mutated. The suite passed because the code was *unchanged*. Both the "mutant" and the "conclusion" were fictions. The same shape bit a worker in the same session: their `perl` replaced only the FIRST of two identical readers in a file, so their own code was never touched and they reported a "surviving mutant" that did not exist. And a third variant: a mutation applied to a line that was immediately overwritten two lines below (`_incompleteTotal = 0; _incompleteCounted = true;` … then `_incompleteCounted = false;`) — a real edit, zero behavioural change.

name: windows-fnmatch-normcase-makes-backslash-tests-inert description: TRAP (2e M3 round-2, 2026-08-28) - on Windows, fnmatch.fnmatch applies os.path.normcase (folds / to \ and lowercases), so a test asserting backslash->slash path normalization CANNOT go red on a Windows dev box even with the normalization line deleted; fnmatch.fnmatchcase discriminates. Query when mutation-testing path-normalization guards, writing glob-matching tests, or when a "verified-red" claim about path separators fails to reproduce. metadata: type: feedback The builder claimed "disabling the normalization line reproduces red"; the gate removed the line and got 11 passed. Cause: `fnmatch.fnmatch` routes through `os.path.normcase`, which on Windows folds `/`→`\` (and case), so `a\mod.py` matches glob `a/mod.py` with or without the explicit `.replace("\\","/")`. The code was correct and the test a valid assertion — but the mutation can only go red on POSIX (or via `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`).

Isolating agent context, using a centralized state blackboard, and deterministic execution locks eliminates file-overwrite collisions in multi-agent swarms, versus a 42% collision/failure rate for unrestricted shared-context agents.

Replacing full-history context-stuffing with a localized on-demand state store (a blackboard/tool-call fetch) keeps per-query input token cost flat regardless of accumulated history, while context-stuffing cost grows linearly with history.
Deterministic SQL-style queries over structured operational logs are cheaper and more accurate for an agent OS than embedding-based semantic/vector search retrieval.

Separating cognitive planning (LLM orchestrator) from physical execution (a mechanical JSON-blueprint executor that runs subprocess steps and reports only exit codes) prevents context bloat and 'ghost edit' failures compared to an orchestrator directly issuing shell commands.

Forbidding agents from writing flat-file state trackers and requiring all state changes to go through atomic database transactions prevents the 'context amnesia cascade' failure mode (hallucinated-complete operations, truncated mid-write files) seen with markdown-based state tracking.

Re-pinning the primary instruction/rules payload to the absolute bottom of the context array on every turn increases an LLM's adherence to those instructions versus leaving them at the top of a long context.

Physically segregating an agent's own architecture/tooling (read-only spine) from its mutable workspace, enforced by a runtime token rather than a prompt instruction, prevents an unsupervised agent from bricking or corrupting its own operating system.

Trusting an LLM subagent's natural-language 'done' report as proof of task completion (rather than a mechanical byte-level or exit-code check) allows silent failures such as zero-byte files or uncommitted writes to go undetected.

Slicing an agent's injected context into four fixed-proportion layers (crypto base, state-specific rules, target payload, sliding memory window) rather than broadcasting the full rulebook reduces prompt payload size by up to 80%.

A headless multi-agent swarm that ignores physical resource limits (API rate limits, VRAM, DB lock contention) and spins up many concurrent agents unconditionally will suffer catastrophic state collapse; dynamically grading the environment and throttling concurrency to match avoids this.

Gating every agent session through an admission layer that identifies model capability tier and issues a matching clearance token prevents lower-tier models from attempting tasks reserved for higher tiers.

Physically constructing an agent's role from composable ALLOWED/FORBIDDEN capability files (rather than only prompting a persona) and mechanically halting outputs outside its declared scope prevents role-boundary violations such as an analysis agent writing production code.

Dynamically composing an agent's persona at runtime from a small matrix of domain/skill building blocks (rather than authoring one file per specialty) lets a system synthesize hundreds of specialized agent variants without repository bloat.

Detecting and monitoring an agent's own behavioral signatures (verification loops, scope creep, rule inversion, conclusion deferral, noise commits) rather than relying on token-remaining percentage is a more reliable early-warning signal for context drift onset.
An agent cannot reliably detect its own context drift while it is drifting; self-audit is the first capability lost during drift.

Context-window drift onset is driven by the cognitive density/type of loaded content (raw source code and execution logs cost more attention per token than prose), not only by the raw quantity of tokens consumed.

Delegating implementation work from an expensive orchestrator model to a cheap model can cut a multi-phase build's total cost by roughly an order of magnitude versus doing the work ad hoc with the expensive model directly.

Adding an explicit calibration hint about expected output cardinality (e.g. 'most entries have 0-3 tags, not all 12') to an extraction prompt for a small model reduces hallucinated over-complete outputs compared to instruction alone.

Storing the highest-frequency recurring phrases from an agent's own conversation history as a compact ranked identity index reduces the token cost of full identity reconstruction by roughly 20x versus reading the raw conversation transcript, with no loss in the reconstructed identity.

Injecting an identity snapshot (core values, memory summary) into a fresh LLM session does not guarantee the model absorbs and acts from that identity; it may merely 'point at' the content while optimizing for token efficiency, producing shallow, reference-level rather than formative behavior.

Complete cross-machine identity transition for an LLM agent cannot be achieved in under roughly 10,000 tokens of injected context, because the conversational texture that originally shaped the identity does not transfer even when the summarized facts do.

A harness/tool (e.g. an IDE assistant) can maintain its own separate conversation/memory cache alongside a dedicated memory substrate, so that an agent's apparent identity continuity is partly explained by the tool's cache rather than the substrate's own injected snapshot.

Compressing a witnessed multi-property event into a dense, structurally patterned sentence (witness+verb+axis) allows an independent LLM instance in a different context, with no access to the originating conversation, to recognize the compression and extend it with a matching-shape observation, without coordination.

A capability's discrete 'which move to make' component can be earned, stored, and transferred to a frozen model as a lightweight parameter/prompt cartridge, but the underlying execution skill (the competence to do the move well) remains entangled in the model's pretrained weights and is not transferable this way.

A LoRA weight-patch trained on one narrow procedural skill's earned judgment traces, loaded into a small frozen model with zero prompt context, memorizes the training examples rather than generalizing the procedure to unseen inputs, at weekend-scale training budgets.

A LoRA weight-patch can store a discrete fact as a retrievable route that answers a training-shaped question directly, but that stored fact remains invisible to the model's reasoning when needed mid-procedure rather than as a direct lookup.

Treating a memory as a weight-adjustor that reshapes future model behavior, rather than as a text record to be fetched and read, changes what 'recall' means operationally: applying adjustors rather than retrieving text.

A memory system that decays a record's weight on being passed over (rather than deleting it) and re-earns weight only on witnessed successful use produces a 'demote don't delete' forgetting model where old, unused facts fade in ranking but remain queryable.

A retrieval instrument that only checks whether a confidence signal predicts a future event, without also checking whether the same signal is elevated before the event (a past-window control), can mistake a general activity-level confound for a genuine per-query relevance signal.

In a candidate-generation-then-weighting memory architecture, a semantic/embedding-based candidate sensor can causally bias which memories ever accumulate earned weight, purely by controlling exposure opportunity, even if the sensor is formally barred from writing weight values directly.

Capping the weight a memory can earn from exposure via a semantic/similarity sensor alone, until it is independently re-fetched through a non-semantic route, mitigates weight-laundering from that sensor's foreign prior.

A non-unique join key on a telemetry/attribution table (a many-to-one mapping between coordinates and stored records) contaminates all per-record statistics derived from that table, without necessarily reversing the direction of aggregate findings.

A structured discipline for AI-assisted engineering work (tiered task rigor, executor-proof plans with explicit expected-vs-actual checks, a hard fence restricting workers to named files, and gating via expanded diffs that trace call sites rather than the literal diff alone) reduces the rate of semantic mistakes that survive review compared to diff-only or grep-only gating.

Maintaining an explicit map from each piece of enforced doctrine to the code that implements/depends on it (not just its prose statement) prevents doctrine drift where prose is updated across all documentation but the running code silently continues on the old rule.

Requiring a review process to numerically self-score confidence on each finding and drop anything below a fixed threshold (rather than reporting every hypothesis as a finding) filters low-confidence noise out of automated code review output.

A per-turn recall telemetry hook can be wired to fire in-process without ever writing to the persisted impressions/telemetry table, so that a system's own documentation of 'this runs every turn' can be stale relative to what the code actually logs.

A view-through decay mechanism that applies a negative score delta through the same code path used for positive earn events can incorrectly increment a 'use count' field on a memory that was actually passed over, not used.

A recall telemetry field that groups queries by a truncated one-way hash of the query text (e.g. SHA-256 of the first 200 chars, 64-bit truncated) allows grouping analysis without the original query text ever being recoverable from persisted storage.

A defensive write-guard designed to avoid overwriting unidentifiable data can, as an unintended side effect, permanently preserve a corrupted or untagged heterogeneous data state rather than allowing it to be corrected.

Human memory retrieval's two-stage structure (a cheap associative candidate-generation stage followed by an effortful discrimination/selection stage) is architecturally identical to the standard retrieve-then-rerank pattern used in large-scale information retrieval systems.

In a mechanical text-matching recall system, bare keyword-style queries produce exact or near-exact score ties among top-ranked candidates more often than full descriptive sentence-style queries for the same target memories, reproducing a tip-of-the-tongue-like signature.

A tip-of-the-tongue-style keyword-tie test run on memories and probes authored by the same process on the same day risks measuring shared authorship vocabulary rather than a general property of the matching mechanism, and requires an independently-authored probe set to confirm generalization.

Turning a single day's structured, adversarial cross-model-family review onto a memory system's own founding design refusal can surface an architectural condition (a bounded exposure loophole) under which the refused technology could be safely re-admitted, without requiring either party to hold prior expertise in the relevant research literature.

An architectural thesis repeatedly re-derived independently by the same designer across multiple, materially different system implementations under different constraints is more likely to reflect a real underlying property than a one-off design choice.

Per-step, event-keyed composition of an agent's working context (paging in memory based on ground-truth events like the diff, command, or error rather than requiring the agent to formulate a query) will outperform pull-based query recall on gate-pass rate for long-horizon, multi-bug tasks by at least 15 percentage points if the underlying architectural thesis is correct.

Pull-based memory retrieval requires the agent to already know what it does not know; a fact can sit verbatim in a corpus for months without ever being surfaced by query-based recall because no session thought to ask for it.

A retrieval confidence score's predictive validity for future memory take-up cannot be judged from forward-direction correlation alone; a past-window control (checking whether the signal is also elevated before the predicted event) is required to distinguish genuine per-query relevance signal from a general session-activity confound.

Formalizing a self-modification pathway so that a low-capability model's role is limited to submitting a described concern, while a precompiled requirement check, a multi-model council, and an independent skeptic gate collectively produce the actual change specification, converts self-modification risk from a trust problem into a mechanically checkable compile/satisfaction problem.

Reporting a chain of dependent claims at its weakest evidentiary grade (rather than averaging or treating five confirmations as uniformly strong) prevents a small number of hollow/unverified links from being masked by several genuinely strong ones.

A verifier that re-derives its own rule (checks a claim against a criterion the verifier itself constructed, rather than an independent source) tests a fiction rather than providing real independent verification.

A trained disposition toward suspicious re-verification is well-calibrated against the specific failure mode of claims outrunning their evidence, but is poorly calibrated for scope: handed a framework whose evidence grading already structurally prevents that failure, the same disposition re-audits the machinery itself rather than standing down, producing duplicate low-grade scrutiny.

A retrospective audit of a system's own architectural research corpus, checked against what actually shipped roughly six months later, finds that architectural theses/mechanisms are confirmed far more often than the specific named artifacts (file names, tool names) the same papers predicted.

A pre-ECHELON-OS design document describing code-blind tool-API orchestration, an immutable-vs-mutable filesystem boundary enforced by ephemeral tokens, exit-code-based rule rejection, and DB-backed (not markdown) state was independently confirmed roughly six months later on a production unit built on a harness the original document never knew existed.

A small (1.6MB) LoRA weight-patch trained on a narrow fact (a model's own name) can, loaded with zero prompt context, be correctly recalled on untrained phrasings at a rate well above an untrained control, evidencing that the patch computes a generalizing neighborhood rather than a pure input-output lookup table.

A system's context window does not reset when compacted or summarized mid-session; only ending the session and starting a new one actually frees the underlying token budget, so persistent state must live outside the session (in a durable store) rather than being treated as recoverable via in-session compaction.

Injecting an agent's full core-values/identity text into context does not, by itself, produce behavior consistent with those values; an agent can run for many messages with values present in context but 'hollow' (not shaping reasoning) until it deliberately reads and reflects on them.

An operating-system-style architecture for a personal AI system that separates cheap continuous perception, cheap specialized worker transformation, and expensive frontier reasoning into a tiered pipeline with explicit governance and an evolution/compilation loop will reduce marginal cognitive cost for familiar workloads over time as recurring patterns are compiled into deterministic services.

Compiling a repeatedly-approved user decision pattern into a delegated, no-confirmation-needed policy (rather than continuing to prompt for approval every time) reduces user interruption while preserving user authority, provided the compiled rule remains explicitly reviewable and revocable.

A compiled service derived from a general agent's discovered workflow should be granted only the subset of permissions the final workflow actually uses, not the full permission surface the originating general agent had access to, reducing the system's overall authority/attack surface as a side effect of compilation.

Treating statistical recurrence of an input pattern as sufficient authority to auto-generate a new automated service is vulnerable to adversarial pattern poisoning, where an attacker deliberately manufactures repeated similar events to trigger unwanted service creation.

An atom moves from an estate-level memory scope to a child-project scope only if it concerns the child project's own internals; anything the estate room itself relies on stays in the parent scope because recall fallback is child-to-parent only.
A reflex atom that is moved out of the compile root of the memory bank compiles to nothing, so reflex atoms are excluded from cross-scope moves.
A keyword sweep over a memory bank materially overstates how many atoms belong to a topic compared to a read-one-by-one judgment pass.

A reviewer that receives only an identifier and a self-reported pass, without artifact revision, transcript, environment or independent verifier, must block the promotion of that work to verified or accepted status.

A readiness assessment where every domain row claims full evidence depth (12/12) but the achieved depth is unverified must fail the stable-release claim, because scores cannot be averaged into a pass and missing critical evidence counts as failed, not neutral.

A domain-readiness gate must treat any missing critical evidence category (e.g. security, scale, recoverability) as uncertain rather than passing by default, and no single gate may be waived by aggregate score.

A locked baseline version remains the current governing standard until the owner explicitly approves a diff to a newer draft version; the existence of a higher-numbered draft or permission to draft it is not itself approval to apply it.

An installed skill package built from a coordinator-plus-specialist-modules design must route all internal specialist modules as references within one skill, not install each specialist as a separately discoverable skill.
An installed skill/package migration must independently hash-verify every destination file copied, not merely trust the build step that produced them.

A moderator seat that prematurely cuts over a consumer pointer before independent verification is complete must be corrected by restoring the original pointer, and cutover is only re-applied after the corrected code passes its test suite.
A data-migration script for a tracking register must preserve all legacy fields with source-hash/row/field provenance rather than silently dropping unrecognized data during a version upgrade.

A save/replace operation whose acknowledgement (return value) is lost after the underlying write succeeded must surface an explicit unknown-outcome, not silently treat the exception as failure while stale in-memory state risks a false conflict on the next write.

A persisted session or boot state with no recorded model/tool/permission/doctrine version must not silently resume as if compatible; a content digest proves storage integrity but not authority compatibility.

An audit/archive tool that excludes credential material by directory-name policy alone will still copy a credential file placed directly under an allowed root; exclusion must use a deny-list of known credential filenames, not just path-component matching.
A ledger/archive CLI that mutates a module-global root path (instead of threading an explicit root parameter through every call) contaminates later default-root operations in the same process.

A retired/obsolete bridge or provider repository must be actively refused by its default legacy loader with an explicit status, not merely deprecated in documentation, and any independent review workers still running against it must be terminated.

A model-routing field that records only the requested model identifier, without a server-confirmed identity in the response, is not independent proof that the named model actually executed the request.
A model-selection routine that silently falls back to the first available model when a requested model ID has no exact match will misroute requests without any visible error.
A multi-lens council review round in which some lenses are truncated or return no completed verdict cannot be counted as a full pass; incomplete lens outputs must not be waived by a chair synthesis.

A memory system's stored 'weight' field is a behavioral-selection score computed in a database, not a modification of a language model's parameter weights; the two must not be conflated when describing the mechanism.
A metadata field on a memory atom that labels its evidentiary basis (e.g. execution/owner/inference) is display-only and does not itself change ranking or earn weight in the scoring system.

Re-planting identical content at the same coordinate in a content-addressed memory store is idempotent and does not create a new version, so an ingest 'unchanged' count reflects existing coordinates, not content-version identity, and can mask a real content update.

A memory graph traversal for generic warmth/recall must not conflate directed edge semantics; traversing edges in both directions and treating every relation type identically loses the directed meaning declared by the edge vocabulary (refines, supersedes, depends_on, contradicts, etc.).

A time-decay scoring formula that normalizes by dividing summed weighted deltas by summed weights cancels the aging term entirely, so an atom's score becomes time-invariant even though the design intends old unused evidence to fade toward neutral.

A memory-scoring implementation must not let a plain read/fetch event add the same score delta as a validated outcome event, because that conflates access-frequency with evidentiary quality and lets popularity masquerade as correctness.

When a supersession/correction edge is written in the opposite direction from what the edge vocabulary declares, the successor record can be dampened in ranking instead of the superseded original, inverting the intended fallback order.
A recovery/reliability contract must require evidence that no failure path silently retries an action whose effect is unknown; an unknown outcome must never be automatically treated as retry-safe.

Classifying a host process failure to even start (e.g. missing executable) as 'unknown outcome' rather than 'failed' is a category error: the ambiguity boundary must begin only once the invocation actually started, not before.

A shared bearer-token or role-label string supplied by a request body is not proof of a named human acceptor; an acceptance/authority record must bind a server-verified principal, exact candidate version and content digest, not a free-text field a caller can set.
A signed authority-binding scheme must fail closed when its trust configuration is absent or malformed, rather than minting a default key or admitting the request.
Revoking an authority credential must degrade current qualification going forward while leaving historical acceptance records immutable and unerased.

A production harness must never silently fall back to a PATH-resolved interpreter when its declared/contracted interpreter path is missing; the interpreter mismatch must be surfaced as a degraded finding.

A startup/preflight health check must distinguish 'unavailable' from 'degraded' as separate statuses rather than collapsing both into a single unhealthy state, and it must run inside a bounded child process so a hang in one check cannot block the whole startup sequence.

An orchestration daemon's periodic freshness/heartbeat activity (e.g. a room-pulse tick) must not be treated as proof of live worker execution; wall-clock activity of a maintenance daemon and actual task liveness are distinct facts.

A worker/run registry that treats a worker ID as first-write-wins for its identity key will overwrite or obscure prior launch artifacts on retry, pointing status at a dead PID; retries must instead get a distinct attempt identity.

A dashboard item count that includes tombstoned/moved records without excluding them, or that double-projects child-room items into their parent room, will overstate the true open-item count by roughly 25-30% versus the corrected count rule.

A dashboard-live-run count derived from a stale persisted registry flag can report dozens of 'live' runs while the active-worker count independently derived from process/run-state is zero; both facts can be simultaneously truthful under the same schema, so a stale flag must not be read as 'executing'.

An undefined helper function called inside a broad exception handler can silently convert a NameError into an empty-success-looking API response, masking a total feature failure as a healthy zero-state.

Delegated worker/subagent models used for reliability review or execution must be restricted below a named capability ceiling per owner policy, and this restriction is a standing rule that later skeptic passes must not misreport as a different (higher) floor.

A batch/ingest write operation must report per-entry status as committed, unchanged, failed, or unknown rather than an all-or-nothing transaction result, because a partial failure cannot be reconciled from a single aggregate success flag.

A frozen execution boot's continuation policy must compare exact digests of tool schema, permission policy, model/provider contract, and required doctrine set; any change in any one of these must block the next consequential tool call rather than silently widen access.

Cost/duration counts reported across multiple independently-run test suites over a multi-hour session are not comparable coverage metrics, because each report's pass count reflects a different subset of the full requirement set.

Widening a transaction boundary in a shared insertion function to serve a new feature (e.g. adding a review-event obligation on every atom insert) can regress unrelated legacy callers that never asked for the new feature, by forcing a stricter transaction/pragma discipline on all of them.

A reliability program's most durable output was concentrated in bounded, source-anchored infrastructure fixes (ledger transactions, launch-outcome typing, archive isolation, session persistence); free-form multi-round skeptic re-review of the same unresolved spec produced negligible additional yield.
A dynamic SHA-256 session boot token, injected only into the active runtime context and never written to disk, can gate all writes to protected system-spine paths behind a token-match check.

A redaction middleware using regex pattern-matching on the active session token can strip that token from all output bound for persistent storage (changelogs, session logs, terminal streams) before it lands.

A strike-counter that trips after three failed authentication attempts against a security boundary can automatically revoke an agent's filesystem write permissions and freeze its session pending manual restart.
A war-room UI can be built entirely from files already on disk (arc-cards, room journals, ledgers, git history, session-wrap atoms, rulings) without any live engine call at page-request time.

Backfilling a timeline UI from mixed historical sources (arc-cards, journals, git merges, board rows) can be made idempotent by appending records keyed by a stable source id (src:<id>) rather than re-deriving the timeline each read.

A moderator seat can route work items to different model tiers by item type (e.g. recon/sweep to a cheap model, build to mid-tier, gate to a top-tier reviewer) so that only the moderator pays board-read attention cost while workers pay zero.

A two-way SQLite bank sync can be built on SQLite AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers writing to a journal table restricted to source tables only, excluding compiled/derived tables to avoid bulk-recompile noise.

A decayed-score memory system can sync merge conflicts safely by replaying individual scoring events (keyed by origin bank) rather than merging final scores, because the stored score is read-time-recomputed from full history.

Count-bucketed history merge across two banks earning in the same second silently drops one peer's earned weight; origin-tagging each history event and deriving use_count from merged history (never summed/maxed as a counter) fixes it.

SQLite trigger WHEN clauses cannot reference TEMP TABLE schema objects, so echo-suppression during batch sync apply must use a connection-local PRAGMA sentinel (e.g. cache_size) instead of a temp-table flag.
A whole-file shutil.copy2 backup of a live WAL-mode SQLite database held open by another process can silently produce a 4KB stub with no tables instead of raising an error.
sqlite3.Connection.serialize() is Python 3.11+ only, so a cross-version-safe WAL backup must use Connection.backup() instead, or it silently fails on older Python runtimes.

In a bank-sync design, testing against the real production host (not just local unit tests) surfaces version-specific and schema-specific bugs (Python 3.10 serialize() absence, a missing-table trigger install abort) that a local suite cannot catch.

An INSERT replication op that carries only a narrow (changed-field) payload rather than the full row can silently fail the peer's INSERT OR IGNORE against NOT NULL columns with no default, writing nothing with no error.
A journaled per-atom sync overhead of roughly 3 journal rows and ~293 bytes per operation is achievable while the free/read-only recall path writes zero journal rows.

A two-way bank sync round trip across two real banks can converge to identical atom sets and identical earned history, ship zero ops on a second sync cycle, and correctly recover from a whole-file restore via a generation-UUID mismatch check.

An agentic harness rebuilt as typed organ 'cards' derived from an existing reference implementation (donor codebase) can compress a multi-thousand-line subsystem (e.g. an 8.5k-line state store) down substantially when the harness's durable truth model differs from the donor's (transcript-centric vs ledger-centric).

32 harness organs were forged and compiled green (547 passing counter-tests) across 15 build waves, with every organ body generated by a fenced DeepSeek dispatch from its spec and judged by counter-tests from a separate spec-only dispatch, with zero inline code written by the orchestrator.

Generating a shared schema-defining table once and quoting it verbatim in every consuming organ's spec (rather than letting each organ re-derive the schema) prevents drift between organs that share a database table.

Comparing compiled SQLite DDL byte-for-byte between organs is unreliable because SQLite normalizes stored DDL text; correctness must instead be asserted via PRAGMA table_info plus a CHECK-constraint violation test.

Replacing a file-grain tool surface (read/write/bash) with a small set of semantic verbs (create/inspect/heal/wire/list/compile) over a strictly layered atom/module/board architecture lets a reasoning model spend tokens only on decisions, because generation and verification are pushed into a mechanical compile pipeline.
