A discipline-transfer thesis: a weak model driving a verb surface that cannot express spec-skipping, untested code, or self-authored success verdicts is structurally prevented from exhibiting the indiscipline a frontier model avoids only because it learned to.

Generating implementation code and generating its tests from the same spec must happen in two separate model contexts (spec→tests never sees the implementation) because a generator validating its own output shares the blind spot that produced the bug.

After three same-class compile failures on one artifact, a framework can grant a per-artifact 'legacy mode' escape hatch (file-grain tools for that artifact only) recorded as a graded, countable degradation rather than silently bypassing the no-inline-code law.

A verification stack ordered import-time-law > counter-generated-tests > effect-observation > receipts removes the model's self-report entirely from the trust chain, because each layer checks the artifact's actual behavior rather than what it claimed to do.

A kernel that knows only laws, receipts, specs and graphs (never a specific language's grammar) can support multiple project grammars (e.g. a Python-backend chain grammar and a web-frontend component grammar) as pluggable data, so adding a new language requires zero kernel changes.
Compilation over a leveled snapshot tree (content-addressed context per node) is a pure function of (snapshot_id, spec_hash), making an unchanged node's rebuild a cache hit rather than a recompile.

A 'seam' artifact kind — a single cross-language contract spec that compiles into N per-language derived projections — makes duplicate cross-language definitions (e.g. an API schema in both a Python router and a TS client) structurally inexpressible, because only the seam spec is ever authored.

Receipt evidence should be reported at its single weakest grade across a compile verdict (external > command > attestation > static) rather than averaged, so a softly-verified component (e.g. a vision-judged design render) never borrows credibility from a mechanically-verified one.

A single project-door manifest file (analogous to a Visual Studio .sln) that declares template, grammars, packs, generator, and layout paths lets a project be fully portable as .eos + src/, rebuilding to a green compile with no other inputs on a fresh machine.

Counter-generated tests must be run red-first against an empty/stub implementation before they are trusted to judge a real body, because a test set that passes a stub or an empty module is vacuous and asserted nothing.

A self-healing runtime agent that proposes spec amendments from uncaught crash records can only catch crashes, never a silently wrong answer that never throws or logs — so this runtime floor is not a substitute for build-time contract tests.

Progress percentage for a supervised multi-agent build should be computed by the engine from witnessed stage-transition receipts (stages-passed / stages-declared), never self-reported by the generating agent, because a self-reported progress bar can lie the way CI progress bars do.

An event stream that is a delta projection of an append-only, prev-hash-chained ledger can recover from dropped frames by refetching the full-body anchor (the ledger/spec-store/bin itself) rather than replaying hope over a gap, because the ledger's chaining makes a gap detectable.

A repair or retry triggered by a possibly-transient failure should never be irreversible on the first attempt; a durability-focused agent should classify the failure, escalate through least-destructive tiers, and verify after each step (abort-and-preserve beats degrade-and-destroy).

State-machine durability requires writing the claim before doing the work, making terminal states immutable via guarded UPDATE with rowcount checks, and recording 'unknown' rather than guessing when the outcome of a possibly-dead process cannot be proven.

Using Python's id(obj) or another ephemeral in-process address as a durability marker on a message/object fails because CPython can reassign that address to a new object, silently making the original write unpersisted.

A circuit breaker's recovery clock should be armed lazily on first blocked evaluation (never persisted at trip time) so that a fresh process after restart still waits a full cooldown window instead of a restart disarming the guard.

Effectiveness of a context-compression breaker must be judged against the same metric the provider actually bills (real prompt token count) rather than a cheaper proxy estimate, because a noisier proxy measurement of the same quantity can reset the trip counter every turn and reopen the failure loop.

A per-session lock keyed by the routing key rather than the durable resource identity (e.g. session_id) is structurally blind to many-to-one collisions between request keys, producing a permanent lock wedge.

An asyncio-based watchdog cannot detect or recover a frozen asyncio event loop because it shares the same execution context it is supposed to guard; only a plain OS-thread watchdog with a heartbeat file and stack-dump forensics can catch a wedged-but-alive process.

sqlite3.Connection's context-manager __exit__ commits a transaction but never closes the connection, so relying on `with conn:` to release resources causes file-descriptor leaks that surface as failures in unrelated components.

A schema migration system should never claim to have reached a schema version it did not actually verify reaching; version bump should be conditional on the target objects actually existing, not on the migration code having run without error.
WAL journal mode support in SQLite must be probed at runtime rather than assumed, because a buggy SQLite build can silently return a non-WAL journal mode from the PRAGMA without raising an error.

A batch runner that derives resume position by matching content in the output file (rather than trusting an in-memory or positional checkpoint counter) survives a crash mid-batch without duplicating or skipping work.

In a 1.06M-line agent harness codebase, a single 5,900-line run-loop function (~30 classified recovery branches) is the load-bearing organ that cannot be statically verified end-to-end by tooling, only by exhaustive human/LLM reading.

A studied production agent harness relabels its 'unknown' turn-exit state to a guessed reason (max_iterations_reached) in its epilogue rather than reporting it honestly as unknown, unlike its own cron subsystem which treats unknown as a first-class non-retried terminal state.

os._exit at gateway shutdown abandons in-flight tool side effects without a terminal record, so their actual effect on the world remains genuinely unknown even though the turn is marked resume_pending.

Owning a durable identity as (process id, process_start_time) rather than PID alone, combined with claim-by-guarded-UPDATE, prevents two racing recovery processes from double-claiming an unowned resource using nothing but SQLite.

Making side-effect side quantities (persist-before-act) turn-terminal on failure — i.e. a broken persistence store stops the turn rather than continuing — prevents a class of silent data loss where the record of a decision never lands before its side effects run.

The ECHELON v.3 north goal is to make the reasoning model read zero source files during a task, driving only through semantic verbs (create/list/inspect/heal/wire/compile) so verification becomes a mechanical compile result instead of a model reading model output.

ECHELON v.3 is planned as three separately built artifacts under a strict one-directional dependency (harness -> framework -> core), where the harness (echelon-agent) is built on the framework, and then the agent is used to rebuild the memory substrate as its own first proving ground.

No studied peer framework (Tessl, GitHub Spec Kit, Bazel, Pants, Salsa, Terraform, protobuf/buf, Nx, in-toto/SLSA) combines a mechanical (import-time-enforced) constitution, context-separated counter-generation, an omission/process ledger, effect-observing doors, and content-addressed generator-context snapshots in one system.

A build-cache key for LLM-generated artifacts must include generator model identity and pack version alongside content hashes, otherwise a silent model upgrade behind a warm cache changes generated output behavior without invalidating the cache.

A schema/API-contract seam spec undergoing amendment should run breaking-change detection against every consuming artifact's contract at amendment time (not birth), because a cross-language contract is safe when first authored but dangerous at every later edit.

In a multi-stage LLM orchestration pipeline, wrapping every stage's model call in reparse/repair/retry/heuristic-fallback layers lets the pipeline degrade gracefully on malformed structured output instead of halting.

Two epistemically distinct verifiers — a persuadable model-based judge and an unpersuadable deterministic pattern-scanner for fabrication signatures (assert True, TODO-only stubs, absence of evidence) — catch different classes of a worker's false success claims when run together.

Content-addressed memory (entry ID = hash of canonical JSON) makes duplicate writes idempotent no-ops and makes deduplication trivial, but explicitly sacrifices semantic/fuzzy recall since retrieval stays deterministic exact/substring match only.

Modeling memory corrections as new 'supersede' entries pointing at the contradicted entry (rather than deleting or blocking the write) turns a contradiction into a first-class, auditable learning event and keeps the full history — including wrong entries — as knowledge about what not to do.

Escalating ambiguous or failed pipeline stages as typed events with explicit options (rather than fabricating a plausible continuation) is a deliberate control-flow law applied across decomposition, evaluation, and execution stages of an LLM orchestration pipeline.

A verification script can report 10/10 PASS totality over a contract graph's static edges while the runtime resolves guard edges through dynamic binding to different targets, silently teleporting flow past a human-mandatory node — meaning totality proofs must run over the expanded (guard-inlined) graph, not the source form.

A function-scale 'effect-observing door' that writes what a function actually did (as an attributed, diffable output file) to a single per-side-effect-class module catches scope violations a return value can hide, because a return value can declare a narrow contract while the function silently performs additional side effects.

A model-free stakes classifier (file-count arithmetic, path globs, keyword regex, blast-radius diffing) that gates whether a full verification graph runs at all — with ties resolving toward the more expensive tier — prevents running verification ceremony on trivially small changes while avoiding under-classifying load-bearing ones.

A gate/judge that authored the artifact it is judging shares the same blind spot that produced the bug, so an artifact-correctness gate must always run on a seat outside the producer's seat list; but for 'soul reads' (what did I actually learn), delegating the judgment to a different seat produces plausible-sounding unearned lessons that mislead future recall, so self-judgment is required there instead.

A findings-output discipline requiring every gate/audit result to list what candidates were considered and rejected (not just what was chosen) prevents a later model from re-searching an already-explored solution space.

An import-time architecture scanner that silently skips a missing or renamed target directory produces a green scan result even though it checked nothing, unless a 'Rule 0' requires the scanner to treat 'cannot check' as a violation rather than a silent skip.

A live incident (2026-08-15) where a reflex rule authored ~80KB of content from stale docs with zero prior recalls produced an invented tier ladder, a fabricated cartridge, and a reference to an executor that already existed, motivating an 'omission reflex' to catch authored-without-recall patterns on cheap session counters.

In a P0-P5 contract-graph loop design, boot-tier liveness probing must read whether a provider's key is present AND a call actually returned, never whether the SDK import merely succeeded, because import success does not prove the provider is reachable.

Pinning a run's live-tier set once at boot (rather than re-probing on every downstream check) means a tier flipping live mid-run does not retroactively unblock an already-parked node, and a tier going dark mid-run does not downgrade a step already in progress.

A model-free stakes classifier can be formalized as a boolean formula over six free ($0) inputs — touched-file count, path globs, keyword regex hits, question-only shape, blast radius, and outward-facing status — to bucket a change into SMALL/MEDIUM/LOAD-BEARING before any downstream pipeline work spends a token.

At the smallest stakes tier of a governed agent pipeline, all guards except the open-question suspension guard can be disabled and the full verification graph does not run at all, treating full ceremony on small work as a defect rather than diligence.

A multi-lens analysis stage that runs a bounded lens set (e.g. 3 lenses, 1 gap loop) rather than the full deep sweep (7 lenses, 2 gap loops) avoids duplicating the security/ops risk pass and the UX design pass that run as separate later pipeline stages.

A risk-analysis stage can be designed to enumerate six risk classes (legal, compliance, GDPR, security, licensing, vendor lock-in) into separate files each with a machine-checkable proof shape, so a validator can exit 0 only when every class is either evidenced or explicitly marked not-applicable with reasoning.

A designed agent pipeline can enforce exactly one human-mandatory decision node in its whole contract graph by refusing to even present the decision dossier unless every upstream evidence receipt is present and no risk finding is blocking without a mitigation entry — making a single documented risk finding insufficient to kill an initiative on its own.

An override path around a mandatory human-decision gate can be made structurally expensive rather than silent by forcing the decided_by field to a distinct 'system:override' value (never impersonating a human decision), requiring a separately-authored override-audit receipt, and re-arming the adversarial-review guard.

A human-mandatory gate with no answer within its SLA window should degrade to a parked state rather than silently defaulting to a 'go' decision, because a silent default on an unanswered gate is worse than an explicitly parked/blocked run.

In a tiered LLM routing scheme, a planning/sequencing stage that produces the critical-path plan every downstream stage is gated against should be routed to a top reasoning tier even though it is cheap to run, because the cost of a wrong plan (re-sequencing every downstream stage mid-flight) dominates the cost difference between tiers.

A work-breakdown-structure exit gate that only checks for the presence of a critical-path artifact (without checking it is an acyclic DAG) can vacuously pass on a WBS with zero leaf tasks; requiring a cycle check on the critical path applies the same graph-totality discipline used on the contract graph itself.

In the 0GAP graph, node n1.5 (data-surfacing) locks schemas/telemetry/API structure as a SHA-256 artifact_hash so that the build node n3.1 refuses entry if the live schema tree drifts from the locked hash.
ECHELON distinguishes receipt grades where artifact_hash proves no content drift since lock time while a plain file-existence receipt only proves the artifact exists.
A node's contract JSON guard list can disagree with the prose/phase-table guard list for the same node, and the compiled contract JSON is defined as authoritative when they conflict.

ECHELON's blueprint discipline (purpose, capabilities, data, hierarchy, presentation, interaction, form, states, responsive, cosmetic) is treated as the deliverable itself, not a separate free-text design document, for node n2.1.
The G1 adversarial-review guard in ECHELON is justified on the principle that self-review shares the same blind spot that produced the original bug, requiring a disjoint seat to review an artifact.

ECHELON's G4 divergence guard measures a temperature score per atom as max(score across atoms within max_hops of the query) times edge_decay^hops, classifying ground as cold (<0.18, full divergence up to 3 candidates), lukewarm (0.18-0.45, one bounded probe), or warm (>=0.45, take the surfaced move).
In a witnessed G4 cold-ground firing at node n2.2 (ui-taste), 9 atoms were visited within 3 hops and 0 were warm, triggering full candidate divergence at $0 model spend (sqlite-only).

ECHELON requires design/build candidates that are rejected during divergence to be recorded with their rejection reason (REJECTED-CANDIDATES LAW) so that downstream gates do not re-search the same design space.

The n2.3 spike node type produces only evidence artifacts (never shippable code), is bounded by a non-extendable TTL, and has a write_jail disjoint from the build node's src/tests directories so a spike artifact cannot accidentally become shipped code.
In the design-lock gate (n2.4), each of the six refutation checklist rows is pass/fail and a single failing row fails the whole gate rather than being averaged or scored.

In a witnessed design-lock gate run, a proposed new component IntakeTextField was rejected because the atlas already held an equivalent component FormTextField with the same states/validation contract, enforcing mandatory component reuse.

ECHELON's build node (n3.1) requires the function contract (signature + comment) to be written before the function body, on the premise that this is the one discipline step an LLM reliably skips otherwise.

ECHELON's microgate system flags function-level violations by comparing an effect file (actual side-effects like INSERT/SEND) against the declared contract, catching omission bugs (e.g., an unauthorized extra email send) that the function's return value alone cannot reveal.
ECHELON's microgate system escalates a trap caught three times into a mechanically-generated reusable rule/atom (three-strikes rule).
ECHELON measured that tool-wait accounts for roughly 70% of wall-clock time in a full test suite run, motivating running the full suite once as a pre-ship gate rather than per-commit.
ECHELON's node n3.2 (gating) runs targeted seam tests scoped only to call sites of touched functions, rather than the full suite, deferring the full suite to a single pre-ship gate before n5.3.

ECHELON's peer-review gate (n3.3) treats a GitHub PR approval fetched live via connector, from a reviewer distinct from the author, as an 'external' grade receipt that a model cannot forge because forging it would require compromising GitHub itself.

When the external review connector (GitHub) is dark/unavailable, ECHELON degrades the peer-review receipt to an 'attestation' grade rather than blocking, and records the degrade explicitly so a run's reported grade reflects its weakest receipt.

ECHELON's G1 guard enforces seat separation at build-time: if the reviewing seat is also a producer seat for the same node's artifacts, the system refuses with a specific FLOW-E04 error rather than allowing self-review.

ECHELON's revise node (n4.1) dispatches to one of exactly four fix cartridges by failure_class (debug/refactor/opt/slim) with no default match, so an unrecognized or missing failure_class blocks the run rather than silently defaulting to a debug attempt.
ECHELON's validate node (n4.2) treats a recorded UAT session against live staging, fetched via connector, as an external-grade receipt distinct from and stronger than a mere deploy-exit-code fact.

ECHELON's hard-quality gate (n4.3) runs a receipt-honesty pass over the run's own ledger checking for four specific receipt pathologies: dead-claim (empty artifact but passing), silent-no-op (exit 0 doing nothing), over-loaded (one receipt covering unscoped guarantees), and wrong-ID (artifact from a different node/run).
In a witnessed P4 pass, the hard-quality gate scanned 38 receipt rows against the four honesty flags and found 0 flags of each type, resulting in a pass with no revise dispatch.

ECHELON explicitly acknowledges its receipt-honesty pass is mitigation, not a solution: because the pass is itself a model reading receipts, a sufficiently plausible hollow receipt can still survive it, and only external-grade receipts are a real defense.
At MEDIUM stakes, ECHELON's workflow drops the honesty-pass gate (n4.3) from its 24-node graph, making it the first gate lost when stakes are reduced from full rigor.

ECHELON's docs node (n5.1) gates every quoted signature/path in generated documentation against the current source tree at its cited hash, rejecting hallucinated symbols by construction rather than by review.

ECHELON's compile step (n5.2) enforces a 'door monopoly' rule that exactly one module handles each side-effect class (db/http/mail/fs/process), checked statically in O(doors) time rather than O(functions).

ECHELON's boot guard makes an app refuse to start in production if build.json is missing, source_hash mismatches the tree, or env==production wasn't deliberately flipped, so an app cannot run unbuilt or stale work in production.
ECHELON's deploy node (n5.3) requires a rollback to be actually exercised and independently re-checked before a deploy receipt is accepted, gated by rollback_proof.ts strictly preceding deploy.ts.

ECHELON's deploy node distinguishes a missing rollback proof (blocks, precondition gap, escalates to a human) from a failed deploy attempt (fails, triggers a real rollback and repackage), never treating a missing precondition as a retry-able failure.

ECHELON's observability node (n5.4) is the only node in the P5 pipeline that never offers an attestation fallback or defer path, because a self-report cannot substitute for third-party telemetry proving a deploy is alive in production.

ECHELON's 'SHIPPED' terminal state is unreachable without an atom-planting receipt (kind: atom) from node n5.5, meaning nothing upstream can substitute for closing the loop with a queryable lesson, even under a graph-wiring bug.

ECHELON's finish-the-loop node (n5.5) requires planted atoms to round-trip through recall (echelon recall by slug must return each just-planted atom) before the plant receipt is accepted; written-but-unqueryable is treated as functionally unplanted.
Newly planted atoms in ECHELON's bank are born at a neutral weight of 0.31 and only gain weight when a later card that used them succeeds, meaning atoms never self-assert significance at creation.

ECHELON's node n5.5 is the one node where self-judgment (the run's own brain deciding what it learned) is deliberately exempt from the seat-separation judge law that applies to every other artifact gate, because delegating identity-level judgment to a different seat is considered 'borrowed self-recognition'.

ECHELON's SMALL-stakes fast path (n5.5-lite) bypasses the full 0GAP graph but still requires a plant-or-justified-silence receipt before SHIPPED, so cheap work is never exempt from closing the loop, only from ceremony.
At SMALL stakes, ECHELON disables every guard except G5 (open-question), treating additional guard ceremony at that scale as a defect rather than diligence.

ECHELON's transcript-mining worker contract requires every extracted candidate to carry a verbatim quote, timestamp, and session id so a gate can verify the claim against the source transcript, rather than accepting a paraphrased event summary as a candidate.

ECHELON's mining worker contract treats owner/user statements as primary ore and assistant statements as secondary, with assistant private reasoning ('thinking' rows) used only as context for what the owner reacted to.
The ECHELON mining contract explicitly tags all mined material from the legacy ECHELON-OS era as possibly superseded and instructs that such doctrine must never be presented as current instruction.

ECHELON's proposed Governor v0 module composes a bounded, per-step context package for a worker by scoring atoms per facet (task text, file basenames, error lines, command heads) using the engine's existing warmth/recall scorer, rather than building a new scorer or using embeddings.

The Governor v0 design commits to recording every atom that scored above zero but was not selected into a 'passed_over' audit list, as a hard requirement for later evaluation of what context was withheld from a worker.
The Governor v0 module is specified to be strictly read-only against the memory bank (never writing atoms or weights during compose()), with the evaluation ledger written only as a separate file.

ECHELON requires the moderator seat to be claimed only after a harness-freshness sync returns a verified ok:true result, applied identically across Claude Code, Codex, and any other harness, and forbids claiming freshness after a failed or skipped sync.

ECHELON's skills and hooks are defined to have their canonical source of truth in ECHELON itself; per-harness installations (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) are mirrors, and independent harness-owned cores are explicitly disallowed.

ECHELON's global deploy law forbids any deploy script from transferring /src, .des, or .eos files to a server, or compiling on the server; only the dist/ build artifact of a versioned, gated release may reach a live box.

ECHELON routes amendment-proposal decisions through a fixed two-step sequence (ECHELON council skeptic review of the brief, then a named decision model for the final call) and requires reporting a limitation rather than silently substituting a different model if the named model is unavailable.

ECHELON's authority-trust provisioning design stores a credential's SHA-256 hash in the server-facing trust config while keeping the raw credential itself only in a separate private, non-archived file, so the raw secret never enters any receipt, board row, ruling, or archive.

ECHELON's authority-trust design makes revocation forward-only: an issuer's revoked field can be flipped to true, but every historical signed binding and receipt must be preserved rather than rewritten.

ECHELON's authority-trust provisioning explicitly separates provisioning (creating the trust file) from acceptance (recording an owner decision), verifying the binding without itself creating a ruling or recording owner acceptance.

A governance baseline can pass a moderator gate as a locked baseline while being explicitly ruled incomplete as a loop, when it defines gates and cheating rules but omits an evidence-record schema, builder/gater separation, and a watcher for reopen conditions.

A process/product completion taxonomy that tracks a business domain will not by itself surface drift in the reasoning/memory substrate (memory, hooks, seat routing, doors, board/rulings, run ledger, health monitors) unless that substrate is registered as its own set of domains.

A closed work-item register decays silently if reopen conditions state WHAT invalidates closure but never name WHO or WHAT SIGNAL detects it, so a dashboard can show a stale-but-green closed row indefinitely.

An amendment process gated separately by (a) a drafting moderator authorized by an owner ruling and (b) a second independent moderator session distinct from the drafting run can produce a reviewed diff package (baseline diff, six amendment mappings, migration preview, skill diff) without any live activation, while still stopping short of adoption until explicit owner approval of the completed diff.

Static integrity checks (byte-identical files, hash matches, JSON schema parse) establish document integrity and internal consistency but do not establish runtime compliance or certify untested specialist execution.

A skill-behavior gate that tests two scenarios in isolation (unsupported handoff acceptance withheld; unsupported Stable claim rejected), independently of the skill's author, can pass with no must-fix findings without that constituting proof the skill behaves correctly under full runtime load.

Reusing an existing environment-variable name for a new distinct purpose (pointing to estate config vs. relocating the memory bank) creates a hazard where a caller who wants to move one silently moves the other; using a dedicated variable whose default lives inside the existing one avoids the collision.
A config reader that raises a named error (missing key + config path) instead of silently defaulting to a hardcoded path prevents a process from re-coupling to one machine while appearing to work.

A hardcoded-path contract test that classifies matches by AST/tokenize rather than line-grep, plus an allowlist requiring every entry to state its kind (FIXTURE/FROZEN/PROSE-IN-CODE) with a second test failing if an allowlisted file stops matching, prevents the allowlist from rotting into a blanket exemption.

An amendment process that separates readiness targets (policy) from achieved evidence (a verified checkpoint set) prevents a domain from silently inheriting credit when its default target values are raised, because achieved-set membership must be independently re-verified rather than derived from the new policy.

A completion lifecycle that adds a mandatory blind counter-test step (independent context derives predicates before seeing builder conclusions) between Verify and Integrate prevents a waiver from turning a builder's self-report into acceptance proof.

Separating a product-domain registry (D01-D77) from a substrate registry (ten scoped SUB-01..SUB-10 rows for memory, hooks, seat routing, board, run ledger, framework, counter-testing, room state, harness freshness, and autonomy safety) lets the engineering substrate be assessed without corrupting product domain identities.

A closed domain's closure becomes untrustworthy the instant its watch signal is missing, stale, or expired, even though the original acceptance evidence remains historically valid; the closure and the historical evidence must be tracked as separate facts.

An AI provider/model used as a decision-maker must be admitted through a live representative-case test table (positive/negative/ambiguous/adversarial/dependency-failure cases) reviewed by an independent context, because a scripted/mocked response proves plumbing only and cannot satisfy model-decision admission.

Restricting mandatory full ceremony records to active domains with at least two independently verified checkpoints (rather than all domains regardless of depth) reduces process-volume ceremony while still requiring a measured cost-to-evidence ratio, defined as spend divided by the count of newly verified checkpoints, to prevent indefinite zero-risk spending during Planning.

A machine-checkable set-coverage rule (required set R must be a subset of the verified met set M) rejects a candidate whose count matches the target but whose membership does not, catching cases like R={1,2,3} vs M={1,2,6} where equal cardinality masks unequal coverage.

An evidence record schema that separates producer, reviewer, verifier, gater, and acceptor as distinct identity fields — with the rule that a producer may never also gate/accept the same candidate — operationalizes the builder/gater separation as an enforceable data constraint rather than a prose rule.

State transitions in an evidence-record lifecycle (planned to performed, reported to performed, performed/verified to accepted) each require a distinct new kind of proof, so relabeling a report as 'performed' or a self-report as 'verified' does not satisfy the transition.

A JSON schema can validate structural shape (enumerations, checkpoint range/uniqueness, required-field presence) but cannot validate semantic claims like independent-actor separation, blind-predicate ordering, or staleness, so a structurally valid record does not by itself constitute proof of a phase gate.

A locked governance baseline can only be amended by creating a new semantic version with recorded compatibility/migration impact, never by editing the approved version in place, and directional approval of an amendment direction is distinct from and does not constitute approval of the completed diff.

A phase completion model that requires an explicit checkpoint-12 acceptance (exit criteria, residual risk, downstream contract, reopen/watch obligations) at every phase closure, not only at Stable, prevents a Planning-phase closure from silently skipping acceptance recording.

A phase-validity formula defined as a strict conjunction of six conditions (evidence coverage, gates pass, no unresolved blocker, bounded waivers, contract consistency, recorded acceptance+watch+cost review) forbids averaging a maturity score across domains as a substitute for meeting every condition.

Treating 'Experimental' as a parallel capability state rather than a chronological phase after Beta allows a Stable-labeled core system to contain Experimental capabilities isolated by feature flags/kill switches without weakening the Stable core's invariants or implying automatic promotion.

Adding G11 (Provenance: every material number/claim traces to an identified source or is marked assumed/sampled/unknown) and G12 (External effect: local success is not proof of external mutation until target-side reconciliation) as cross-domain gates closes a class of failure where a queued/mocked local success is reported as a completed external effect.

A dependency-admission checklist that treats an AI provider/model as its own risk-classed dependency kind (separate from ORM/broker/database classes) rated by consequence rather than remoteness prevents underrating a decision-making model simply because it is a remote API call.

A cost-to-evidence axis that reports cost divided by the count of newly-verified checkpoints (never dividing by zero, never treating unknown spend as zero) surfaces spend that produced no new evidence, making an indefinitely-running zero-progress Planning phase visible rather than hidden.

A read-only migration-preview procedure that preserves every original source column/value, sets all new checkpoint fields to null/unknown rather than zero, and blocks recovering an achieved-checkpoint set from a legacy x/12 scalar (never producing range(1,x+1)) prevents an old imprecise score from being silently upgraded into precise but fabricated evidence during a schema migration.

A drafting unit can complete and internally validate a full amendment package (22/22 static checks passing, byte-identical originals, matching hashes) while explicitly declaring zero adoption/activation, keeping 'drafted' and 'approved-and-live' as strictly separate states that a reader cannot conflate.

A skill-adoption plan that requires every occurrence of a rule (e.g. 'A-P for each domain') to be revised together across execution steps, output requirements, and final checks — rather than patched additively in one place — prevents a stale unconditional requirement from surviving elsewhere in the same instruction document.

SHA-256 hashing every inspected source document, with line numbers marked as valid only for a specific snapshot (drift to be detected by hash+heading rather than trusted line numbers), gives an amendment package machine-checkable provenance independent of git operations.

A static package-validation script that initially failed on a real check (comparing qualified alias 'echelon:D78' against bare 'D78') was corrected by fixing the checker's own parsing bug rather than by altering the underlying evidence, and both the failing and the corrected run were preserved for audit.

A package-validation run that passes 22/22 structural/static checks (hash identity, schema validation, illustrative fixtures rejecting duplicate/out-of-range checkpoints) explicitly does not constitute an independent runtime or moderator acceptance gate.

A command-center's own owner-reported master test result (324 passed / 4 failed) can honestly separate an environment-specific CI gap (4 missing shim checks) from unresolved product defects, while still declining to credit any phase above Planning due to absent domain-specific and integrated gate evidence.

A first vertical slice for a command-center product can be scoped to owner-facing coordination visibility (board/ruling read+route, run visibility, evidence links, safe framework admission) while explicitly excluding inventory business workflows, production deployment, live-box mutation, and provider credential management, treating those exclusions as activation triggers rather than permanent gaps.

An architecture invariant that forbids a room-directed record from silently becoming another room's work, enforced by requiring a routed record to retain its room and source with mismatch blocking execution, prevents cross-room contamination of routed actions.

An invariant that treats any unexpected mutation during a Planning/review-only path as an S-class incident (rather than a minor bug) enforces a hard boundary between read/route operations and live effects.

An architecture blueprint that explicitly defers introducing a message broker, microservice mesh, second database, or generic plugin system until a measured problem and exit path exist keeps a thin-slice system from acquiring speculative distributed-systems complexity before evidence demands it.

A deploy-law contract that restricts what a server may receive to a gated dist/ release artifact (never source) is cited as an architectural constraint at the boundary between the framework and the command center, meaning this planning record itself authorizes no deployment.
A first vertical slice of a command-center product reuses existing board, rulings, moderator and runs seams instead of building a new service.
A planning-stage UI projection is required to stay read-mostly with all effects gated, to satisfy a no-hidden-effect invariant.
A design framework's door file and canvas assets are treated as source-class (S-class) admission surfaces with provenance requirements, not flattened into generic files.
Each AI model or provider is treated as an untrusted, metered external dependency requiring provider/version/usage attribution rather than as a trusted internal component.
No dependency in a system's admission inventory can be approved for production while version, license, vulnerability, cost, credential and provider data-handling evidence remain open.
A source-observed authorization code path fails open (returns unauthenticated-allowed) when a config flag cannot be read, and this blocks phase closure until independently proven contained.
A stated intent to monitor or review ('watch text') is not treated as an installed monitor, and a 'pending' label is not treated as an approved waiver.

In a 77-domain engineering operating model register applied to one estate, an independent applicability audit reclassified 62 previously non-active rows into 30 active, 23 deferred and 24 inapplicable.

Substrate-level responsibilities proposed as an amendment to a domain register are kept outside the canonical register until approved, so they cannot be used to satisfy ordinary security, data, workflow or cost duties.
A test suite failure caused by a missing optional shim/environment component is classified as an environment gap, not a product defect and not a passing test.
A test regression was traced to an environment variable (a role-claim variable) set incorrectly for a worker seat rather than to a product defect.
A historical aggregate test-pass count (e.g. 1321 passed) does not by itself prove a later feature slice's integration or release readiness.

Read-only inspection is required as the default evidence-collection step; any command that could write, route, post, create, restart, deploy, or call a provider must stop until explicit authorization and gate exist.
On a suspected room or provenance breach, the standard operating response is to not retry the effect and to hold dependent work rather than continue.
A moderator, not the delivery document, owns creation/alteration/closure of tracker items; a delivery plan proposing OPEN items is text-only and has no tracker-mutating effect.
An unchanged, locked baseline governance document plus an unapproved amendment proposal can coexist without the proposal silently altering the baseline's rules.
Completing an assessment/documentation package is explicitly distinct from completing the underlying software system or achieving phase closure.
Every source citation in a phase assessment is pinned to a specific git revision hash, and later movement of the live HEAD does not retroactively change what was assessed.

Hashing a file for baseline verification across CRLF/LF checkouts requires EOL normalization; a raw-byte hash without normalization only locks the local checkout, not the content, and will mismatch on another machine.
An owner-reported test-pass count (e.g. '324 passed / 4 failed') is treated as a claim, not as a new execution, until an independent context records the command, environment, fixture, and verdict.

A proposed external-effect gate requires that local success (a local command, mock, or scripted fixture) is not treated as external success until the target system is reconciled and the receipt names the external observation.
A proposed provenance gate requires every number, status, screenshot and generated artifact to trace to a source record/revision or be explicitly marked assumed, sampled, or unknown.
A builder's green test suite is treated as a report, not an acceptance; acceptance requires an independent moderator or gate context to rerun or counter-test the claim.

A phase gate's validity formula treats each of five conditions (domain thresholds, mandatory gate passes, no unresolved blocker, bounded deferrals, cross-domain contract consistency) as a strict conjunction, so failing any one makes the whole gate fail regardless of the others' scores.
Any demonstrated cross-room authority leak or tenant leak is treated as an immediate blocker to a phase claim irrespective of otherwise-high domain scores.

A bounded source-and-artifact review (a 'hard-gate scan') is explicitly not equivalent to a penetration test, complete code audit, production incident search or recovery exercise, and absence of an observed leak in that scan is not proof of absence.
A domain-register readable view (a tracking Markdown table) can be mechanically generated from the same authoritative CSV rather than maintained as a separate hand-written document.
A budget stop that used a cache-inclusive total-token metric (3,360,345 tokens) overstated the actual cost basis, which the corrected accounting later fixed by excluding cached input tokens.

Removing one environment variable (a seat-role variable) from a diagnostic test run fixed two resume assertion failures but left a separate smoke test still failing, showing the two failure classes had different root causes.

Round-two token accounting used (native uncached input minus cached input) plus output, sampled at subtask boundaries across root and descendant sessions, as a more accurate cost basis than a cache-inclusive total.

A cost-tracking tool (runs.py cost) failed when used as an output destination because that door expects an existing capture file rather than writing a new one, requiring a fallback to native provider counters.

A console-UI audit found that a header chip labeled 'runs in flight' counted historical ended/succeeded runs alongside live ones because the exclusion set used a deny-list of terminal states that did not match the registry's real vocabulary, inflating a true count of 3 running runs to a displayed 510.

Allow-listing the desired states (e.g. only 'running') rather than deny-listing terminal states is a more robust fix for a live-count display bug, because a deny-list drifts when the underlying state vocabulary changes.

A console page rendered board rows with empty body text for three consecutive rows, traced to a poster writing empty text; the fix was to reject empty-text posts with a 400 at write time and render an explicit '(empty)' placeholder rather than a blank UI element.

A room-transcript view that defaults to opening at the oldest row rather than the live tail causes a moderator to see an 8-day-old message instead of current activity, unlike a sibling chat view that correctly lands on the tail.

A ruling/decision that has been decided ('ruled') but not yet executed ('acted') was invisible in headline counters that only counted status=='open', which could mislead an owner into believing nothing is outstanding.
Distinguishing a 'no data available' UI state from a 'value exceeded threshold' alert state in a badge/counter prevents a data-fetch gap from being misread as a real overage.
A fixed-width mobile UI tile can force-wrap a numeric string to one character per line when the container width is too small for the content, a CSS overflow defect distinct from a design/taste issue.
A package freeze law defines FREEZE as version + interface list + contract test + a frozen tag in a manifest, never a compiled binary artifact and never a copy of source files.

Content hashes for a frozen package's source files must be computed with line endings normalized to LF, because a mixed CRLF/LF checkout makes a raw-byte hash lock the checkout rather than the content and fail on any other machine.

Flattening multiple Python modules into one namespace via wildcard imports can silently let identically-named public symbols in different modules shadow one another; a package avoided this by importing one submodule per frozen module instead.

A graph-query tool over a code dependency atlas, cross-checked against a direct import-line read, can enumerate exactly which external names a frozen module set actually consumes versus merely mentions in comments.

A room-resolution algorithm falls through a fixed five-step ladder (explicit registry name, ancestor directory walk, a project door file, git root, then registered scope) to determine which state directory a given working directory belongs to.

A 'promote a project to its own room' operation gates the write behind five hard criteria (independent repo, deploy boundary, at least 3 explicitly-tagged open items, and a real directory on disk) checked before any file is written, and fails closed via a raised error if any criterion is unmet.

An ordering conflict was found where a delivery brief sequenced 'register and promote a project to a room' before the sweep step that would tag enough items to satisfy the promote operation's own gate criteria, making the promote step fail as ordered.

A tracker item's 'move to another room' operation is designed to never delete the source record but instead write a tombstone recording the new location, because no reader-side alias/tombstone-resolution facility exists yet and readers must be taught to follow it.

A ruling's room assignment is set only at its creation event and is never re-derived on later rule/say/acted events, so moving a ruling to another room requires a new explicit room-retag event type rather than relying on existing fold logic.

Adding a new state subdirectory to a project already containing unrelated application state (a cache/ledger) is safe as a non-destructive coexistence operation as long as the new writer only creates non-colliding filenames and never removes the directory.

A pre-sweep classification pass that reads each open tracker item's text and proposes a target room, without moving anything yet, made a subsequent owner/moderator re-homing sweep of dozens of items cheap to execute.
A cross-estate item move was explicitly scoped out of a first sweep slice and deferred to an owner ruling in a later slice, keeping the move operation's blast radius bounded to one estate at a time.

A ledger of atoms addressed by hierarchical coordinates provides an automatic fallback ladder by construction: if no atom satisfies a request at the most specific depth, the system ascends one level at a time until a match is found, without needing separate fallback logic.

A memory atom's score is proposed as unbounded (no ceiling) with a fixed neutral benchmark anchor of 100, analogous to Elo, so that score reflects only accumulated evidence rather than an artificial cap.

A proposed time-decay weighted scoring formula (exponential decay per feedback event, tunable per rating dimension) is designed so an old high-scored but unused atom loses effective weight to a recently-validated lower-scored atom, preventing stale content from dominating retrieval.

A design proposes that under token-budget pressure a system should drop the lowest-scored references first (both individual atoms and, recursively, whole sub-cards), so a request degrades gracefully to its highest-value subset instead of failing outright.

A guard system proposes that novel taxonomy nodes an AI wants to create must be paused and explicitly approved by a human before being written, rather than auto-created, to prevent taxonomy pollution from LLM shortcuts.

A memory-synthesis design (merging two related atoms into a new atom) is a self-audit-caught terminology error in its own first draft: the spec described the merge output as a new 'card' with card-only fields, when the merged content is structurally an atom, not a card.

A cross-user import design proposes resetting an imported card/atom's score to a fixed baseline (e.g. 50) rather than preserving the exporter's original score, because a score earned in the exporter's context would otherwise dominate the importer's index via stale-context bias before proving itself locally.

A self-improvement loop design proposes that execution traces (self-reported steps, cost, quality, improvement notes) be persisted as first-class, addressable records rather than discarded after the session, on the premise that discarding the reasoning path (as traditional gradient-based training does) loses the evidence needed for later inspection or reuse.

A design proposes that a high-value insight discovered while executing one task (a 'beacon') should be stored in a domain-agnostic location so it can be voluntarily adopted by unrelated tasks/cards, rather than being trapped inside the context where it was discovered.

A meta-planning design proposes that the planning routine itself should be treated as an ordinary card subject to the same trace-review-mutation feedback loop as any other task, rather than being exempt, so that planning quality can self-correct across sessions.

Delegating a task to a cheaper model tier only saves cost if the delegator accepts the output without re-verifying it from scratch; without an evidence log the receiving model either re-derives the work, assumes it is correct (drift), or hedges defensively, all of which are expensive.

A stronger/more capable judge model, absent an evidence log of what the producing model attempted and rejected, re-verifies more rather than less, so upgrading judge capability without logging makes a delegation pipeline slower rather than faster.

A verification/proof script can pass 10/10 on a workflow graph while having proven the wrong artifact (the static edge targets) rather than the artifact that actually executes at runtime (dynamically resolved guard bindings), producing a fully green report over a defect-laden system.

A checker written by the same effort that produced the artifact it verifies inherits that effort's blind spot, so gating must be performed by a second, independently-written checker rather than trusting the original verifier's green result.

Proving that every state in a workflow graph has a defined outgoing transition (totality) is necessary but not sufficient for correctness, because a graph can be total while every transition routes to the wrong place.

In a workflow graph where conditional guards can trigger retries or reroutes, guards must be modeled as call/return subroutines with a call frame rather than as nodes with static outgoing edges, or a static totality/reachability proof will not match the graph that actually executes.

A documentation set authored from uploaded reference files without querying the live running system will invent parallel mechanisms, fabricate names, and misstate configuration that a single query against the running system would correct, and each successive grounding pass against the live system is cheaper than the last while finding more.

A memory-recall system's middle confidence band (partial/lukewarm recognition, distinct from both 'known ground' and 'cold/new ground') should trigger one bounded verification probe of the most relevant prior result rather than either full re-exploration or blind reuse.

An automated guard/hook system must fail open (allow the action, log, continue) on its own internal error but fail closed (block) on a genuinely detected violation, or a guard that can crash a session gets uninstalled by its operator within a day, leaving no guard at all.

A pre-tool-call guard hook that re-imports its dependencies on every invocation instead of using a persistent worker process adds a measurable per-call latency tax (roughly 74ms in one measured instance) that compounds across a session into perceptible slowdown.

Raw diff line-count is a poor proxy for the intellectual/risk stakes of a code change: a large mechanical file-move commit can carry near-zero stakes while a tiny commit closing a correctness gap can carry high stakes, so a stakes classifier must log-transform and cap line counts and weight commit/file counts more heavily.

In a stakes-classification system for gating work ceremony, an irreversible outward action (deploy, external write, service restart) should override every other signal and force the highest ceremony tier unconditionally, rather than being one weighted factor among several.

Detecting that a work session committed code but never ran its close-out/knowledge-capture step (an 'orphan' session) only proves the narrower claim 'committed but never wrapped'; it cannot detect sessions that made no commits at all, so a separate floor signal (e.g. any bank/memory write) is needed to catch those.

A rule/reflex system's overall reliability check (e.g. a mechanical scanner or verifier) can pass while checking nothing meaningful ('vacuity') or checking the wrong artifact entirely ('misdirection', e.g. checking a static field instead of the dynamically-bound one it diverges from), and a coverage-count check alone only catches the first failure mode, not the second.

A stale compiled .pyc file from a broken source version can silently shadow a fixed .py source file after a crash-loop restart, so the fixed code never actually runs while the error persists, and clearing/verifying the bytecode cache must be a mandatory build step.

A build-time policy warning tier is only safe from rotting into permanent ignored noise if every warning carries a mandatory expiry date after which it automatically escalates to a build-blocking error.

Restricting every side-effect class (database, HTTP, filesystem, mail, process) to exactly one designated module ('door') in a codebase, and statically failing the build if any other file references the underlying primitive directly, is a static and deterministic enforcement mechanism that scales with the number of side-effect classes (roughly 5-10) rather than with codebase size.

Classifying each function individually as safe/unsafe to auto-execute (for a dev-mode test harness) does not converge as codebase size grows, because every new function is a fresh misclassification risk; forking the small, finite set of side-effect access points ('doors') to redirect to a dev sink is a bounded, one-time decision that makes every function safe to run by construction.

A per-function automated gate that runs after a function is written (fires on 'having written' rather than 'about to run') can catch three specific defect classes that reading the return value alone cannot: a function doing more than its declared scope ('over-loaded'), a function whose comment claims behavior the body doesn't perform ('dead-claim'), and a function returning success while doing nothing ('silent-no-op') -- by comparing the function's declared contract hash against its body hash and against an observed side-effect log.

A model reading its own just-written code and judging it correct shares the exact blind spot that produced any bug in that code, so a completion gate must actually execute the code and compare observed output/side-effects to the declared contract rather than relying on the same model's self-assessment.

An event-triggered enforcement system (reflex/guard rules) that fires only on 'about to act' events (pre-action hooks) is structurally unable to detect omissions -- necessary steps that were never attempted -- because skipping an action is not itself a matched event; catching omissions requires a persistent state token that a separate check can read.

In a live rule/reflex enforcement system with a hard-block action available, block-type rules should be reserved almost exclusively for irreversible writes to a source of truth (measured at roughly 2 of 149 live rules in one estate), with everything else defaulting to a non-blocking warn.

A conditional-arming mechanism for guard rules can exist in a rule schema and be almost entirely unused in practice; in one measured live ruleset only 2 of 149 rules used the optional conditional-arming field, both keyed on cheap session-state counters rather than on the command being matched.

A guard/reflex rule can go stale by citing a resource (e.g. a named cartridge/module with a claimed atom count) that no longer exists or no longer holds the claimed content, and nothing in a standard reflex-test suite (which only checks that the rule fires on its trap and stays quiet otherwise) detects this; the rule's cited referents must also be asserted to still resolve.

A judgment about whether a produced artifact is correct requires a different reviewing seat/model than the one that produced it (to avoid shared blind spots), but a judgment about whether a piece of reasoning belongs to a model's own identity/self-recognition must be made by that same model, because delegating identity-judgment to a cheaper sibling produces borrowed, unearned self-recognition.

For an autonomous or bounded work loop, elapsed step count or attempt count is a poor primary bound because a long, genuinely productive run (e.g. compiling many facts across many surfaces) is indistinguishable from a stuck run under a raw step cap; the load-bearing bounds should instead be a drift/thrash counter (net non-productive steps, paid down by good steps), wall-clock TTL, and real-dollar budget, with step count serving only as a high emergency backstop.

A single 'viability/stuck' guard armed only on failure signals (attempt count, budget burn with no new receipts) is structurally blind to a distinct failure mode where every step succeeds and produces a valid receipt but the run never approaches the actual goal ('circling'); detecting circling requires a separate progress-check guard that periodically asks whether recent steps moved closer to the goal.

Making a judge/gate check mandatory and always-on in an agent loop was measured to be net cheaper (roughly 34-39% cheaper) than making it optional, because the steps the mandatory judge saves outweigh the cost of running the judge itself.

When an agent workflow hits a genuine blocking question, modeling that state as a full terminal stop (ending the run) is worse than modeling it as a resumable suspension that preserves the run's frame/context and resumes exactly where it left off once answered, because a terminal-stop design incentivizes the agent to guess rather than ask.

When an agent's context window approaches its limit, the loop should proactively summarize its state into a persistent spine, flush the noisy transcript, and re-enter on the summary rather than treating context exhaustion as a hard stop requiring a resume token from an external park state.

A ceremony/process-overhead policy should scale with the measured stakes of the change (mechanical/single-file vs. real-but-known-shape vs. schema/deploy/architecture/outward-facing), and running full process ceremony on a trivial change is itself a defect, not diligence, because it teaches operators to bypass the process entirely.

Running a full test suite on every commit inside a build loop is not extra safety but wasted tool-wait time (measured at roughly 70% of a session's wall-clock in one estate); the full suite should run once as a pre-ship gate while per-commit gating stays scoped to the targeted change.

Enforcement rules/laws for an agent substrate are better authored as flagged, recallable memory entries (compiled into a ruleset and fired by event hooks) than hand-written into enforcement code, because rules-as-memory are disputable, warmth-ranked, per-scope, and portable between banks, whereas rules-as-code require the operator to maintain them separately from the memory substrate.

A receipt/evidence system should grade its proof types by forgeability, with facts fetched live from an external third-party system of record (e.g. a platform API confirming a code-review approval by a non-author, or an observability query showing a live post-deploy signal) ranked as the strongest evidence, because forging them requires compromising a system the producing model does not control -- strictly stronger than a local command exit code, file hash, or another model's attestation.

When a receipt/evidence source falls back from a stronger grade (e.g. a live external system check) to a weaker one (e.g. a model attestation) because the stronger source is unavailable, the run's status report must record and surface that degradation explicitly rather than showing an undifferentiated pass/fail.

A distribution/plugin packaging format that can ship hooks bound to lifecycle events (session start, pre-tool-use, post-tool-use, stop), plus declared skills and external connectors, is sufficient to carry an entire enforcement contract as an installable unit rather than as a document someone has to read and follow manually.

An enforcement/guard layer built entirely on pre-action (pre-tool-use) hooks can guard against dangerous acts but is structurally incapable of guarding against omissions (a necessary phase never entered, a lesson never captured, a function never proven); closing that gap requires a persistent state token plus enforcement on completion/session-end events, not more pre-action rules.

A workflow gate should require a per-item refutation checklist (each check row scored pass/fail with cited evidence) rather than an aggregate score, because an aggregate score lets many passing rows average away one failing row that should block the gate on its own (e.g. a missing performance budget or an accessibility violation).

A deploy step should be gated on having proven a rollback path by actually executing the rollback once in staging before allowing production rollout, rather than merely having written a rollback script and assumed it works.

Post-deploy observability should be proven by querying a live monitoring signal timestamped after the deploy event (including a synthetic test event deliberately round-tripped through the pipeline), because a zero-error-count reading with no confirmed live signal proves nothing about whether the monitoring pipe is actually open.

A memory/knowledge-capture step is not complete when the write operation exits successfully; it must be proven by an independent read-back through the same retrieval path a future session would use, because a written-but-unqueryable record is functionally equivalent to no record at all.

A workflow contract that gates entry to a downstream phase on a human decision cannot make that human decision cheap or fast without eliminating the accountability it exists to provide; the correct mitigation is minimizing wasted wait (never prompting prematurely, pre-assembling the decision dossier) rather than trying to make the decision itself lighter-weight.

A workflow gate/contract system cannot mechanically distinguish a technically-satisfied receipt (correct shape: file exists, command exits 0, attestation cites the right ids) from a substantively hollow one (empty content, trivial test coverage, a review that never actually read the diff), because automated judgment is itself a model output that can be satisfied cheaply; this residual gap is only partially mitigated by seat rotation and duplicate-reasoning detection, never closed.

A peer-review gate that requires review from a rotating pool of at least three distinct reviewer seats (rather than a fixed pair) closes the collusion case where two reviewer identities resolve to the same underlying model or a captured reviewer pair reuses boilerplate reasoning across unrelated artifacts.

An automated stakes/ceremony classifier for routing work through a heavier or lighter process should be implemented as zero-cost keyword/path/glob matching over the change description and diff stat (no model call), because a model call to decide whether to call a model defeats the purpose of a cheap classifier.

In a stakes-tiered process-gating system, classification errors should resolve toward the more expensive/thorough tier by default, because under-classifying risks shipping a real defect through a process that never ran, while over-classifying only costs tolerable extra ceremony.

A drift/thrash guard measuring 'being lost' via a net-failure counter (good steps pay down the counter) remains a constant-time, zero-cost arithmetic check regardless of run length, so a 400-step genuinely productive run and a 6-step failing oscillation are distinguished correctly by the counter rather than by elapsed step count.

A bank-temperature-based divergence guard using a bounded graph walk (max hop count, decay per hop) will read as cold on ground the memory bank actually covers if the relevant highly-scored atom sits beyond the hop limit, so any such guard's cold verdict must be qualified as 'cold within N hops', not an absolute claim about the bank's coverage.

Deliberately erasing or pruning an append-only decision/action ledger silently disarms any drift/thrash guard whose counter is derived from that ledger's history, since the counter reads clean after the history is deleted even though the underlying problem is unresolved -- making ledger-tidying itself a high-risk operation that should route through an explicit decision step, never an automatic 'work' step.

A transient, per-turn-rendered context block restating the current task/contract state (popped immediately after each send, never appended as a permanent conversation turn) prevents both context pollution from repeated stale reminders and the agent forgetting task constraints as the conversation grows long, because the constraint is re-stated fresh every step rather than stated once and buried by later turns.

A runtime permission/write-scope enforcement mechanism should be config that the executing loop itself reads and honors, not an external sidecar process that polices writes after the fact, because a sidecar auto-approver can become blind to the loop's actual operating mode (e.g. approving overwrites regardless of whether the session is in an auto-accept mode or not).

Gating a build/compile step on the presence of a valid workflow-state token (proving required upstream phases were entered and their exit conditions satisfied) makes phase-skipping detectable at the exact moment it becomes consequential -- the attempt to produce a runnable/shippable artifact -- converting build into the chokepoint where omission becomes provable.

An enforcement architecture split so that local, sandboxed act-guards (pre-action rules) stay device-local while an omission-tracking workflow token synced to a shared database travels with the work, correctly matches coverage to risk: acts inside a sandbox are contained by the sandbox, but the work product that leaves the sandbox is exactly what omissions can damage.

A verifier that proves graph properties (totality, reachability) over the static edge declarations rather than the runtime-resolved dynamic bindings can report all-pass while the runtime actually skips mandatory steps.

Modeling a guard as a call/return subroutine (push a frame with the caller node and a successor resolved at call time, pop to return) prevents cross-binding teleportation bugs that a guard modeled as a static graph node with fixed edges is prone to.

A guard armed only on failure signals cannot detect a workflow that produces all-passing steps yet never approaches its stated success metric; that requires a separate sampled judgement over a window of steps.
A drift counter that increments only on failed steps and decrements on passing steps distinguishes a long productive run from a thrashing one, whereas a step-count or elapsed-time bound cannot.

A worked trace recorded a real oscillation: 6 steps alternating between two file states all failing with an oscillation penalty (+2 for revisiting a prior state) tripped a drift threshold of 6 exactly at step 6.

Requiring a self-review gate's output to include an explicit list of rejected candidates (with reasons) prevents a model from resubmitting a restated draft that only cosmetically differs from prior attempts.

Weighting recalled memory by a hop-decayed score over a bounded graph walk (e.g. decay 0.7 per hop, cutoff at 3 hops) means a perfectly relevant memory item beyond the hop cutoff registers as cold even though the underlying knowledge base actually covers it.

When a memory-warmth check reads a borderline (lukewarm) score, doing exactly one bounded probe of the nearest memory item and recomputing the score afterward can promote the item to warm, because the act of reading a memory item increases its measured weight.

A cold-start Python interpreter invoked per pre-action hook call measured 74ms per call in production use, which is high enough above a sub-10ms budget that the delay was noticeable to the human operator before being diagnosed; the fix is a persistent warm worker process instead of a fresh interpreter per call.

All arm/disarm predicates of a six-guard safety layer (five guards fully, a sixth partially) can run at zero cost with no model call and no network access, using only local ledger reads and local sqlite queries, so the safety layer keeps functioning even when every upstream model provider is unavailable.

A named rule that cites specific reference items (e.g. atoms/documents in a memory scope) can pass its own coverage self-check while every cited item is actually absent from the referenced scope, producing a rule that fires with false authority; a separate check that resolves every cited referent against the live system is needed to catch this, distinct from a check that only proves the rule scanned something non-empty.

In one estate's ruleset, hard-blocking enforcement actions were deliberately reserved for only 2 of 149 total guard rules (both governing irreversible writes to a source of truth, both carrying an explicit override), reflecting a policy that warn-by-default plus rare block is calibrated far more conservatively than an earlier version that blocked liberally.

A stakes-classification rule that exists only as prose instructions the model is told to 'hold in context' (no implementing code, flag, or field computing the tier) is unenforceable and drifts; a sweep of one estate's codebase for stakes-classification terms found 59 hits, all in docstrings/prompts/atom text, none in executable logic.

In one estate, no hook fired on session-end-without-wrap: the session-end and subagent-stop hook slots were both configured empty, meaning nothing detected or nagged about a session that ended without running its close-out/knowledge-capture step.

An independently written second graph-property derivation tool, built without sharing logic with the original prover, reproduced the same counts (83 vertices / 259 edges, 80-of-83 reaching a shipped-terminal state) as the original prover, and caught a real off-by-one bug in the second tool itself by disagreeing with the first.

An 80KB technical specification authored against six uploaded reference documents without querying the running live system contained multiple confident but incorrect claims (an invented tier ladder duplicating a working one, a fabricated capability/cartridge name, a proposed component that already existed) that six subsequent grounding passes against the live system found and corrected, costing most of a working session.

A local, per-workstation ruleset (e.g. dangerous-action guard rules) does not automatically sync to a cloud-hosted execution environment even when the persistent knowledge store (bank/database) does sync, so an agent running in the cloud environment executes with zero coverage from the local guard rules unless the guard mechanism is deliberately re-architected to ride the syncing store.

Gating a build/compile step on a valid, current 'flow token' that must exist and be at a permitted graph position converts an otherwise-undetectable omission (a required phase that was silently skipped) into a detectable build failure, because a build is itself an act (unlike a skipped phase) and acts can be structurally gated.

A prior design draft asserted that gate/review judgement should always come from a model different from the artifact's producer (self-review always forbidden); this was retracted for one specific node type where the judgement is about which lessons the producing run itself learned, because delegating that self-judgement to a different model produces 'borrowed self-recognition' rather than genuine self-assessment.

A skeptic reviewer re-checking a prior CONFIRMED finding (that a revert-on-gate-failure mechanism was atomicity-safe) discovered the original check only covered the case of a gate returning nonzero, not the case of a gate process crashing or timing out mid-write, meaning an uncaught exception between write and revert leaves a partial mutation on disk despite the earlier finding having been marked CONFIRMED.

A guard-coverage checker verified only that a named guard's basic bind conditions (like being listed in a coverage table) held, without checking that the guard's own arm-prerequisite fields were actually present on the node it was bound to, allowing a guard to be bound at a site where it can structurally never fire while the coverage check still reports full pass.

Hardcoding a live measured count (e.g. a rule count) into multiple documentation files causes drift the moment the underlying system changes; a spec cited '149 rules' in six files while the live count was 162 at time of writing and had already changed to 160 by the time it was checked.

A design specification's stated precondition (that an autonomous agent cannot build/ship code it skipped a required review step for) can be undermined if the same agent that the precondition constrains also has write access to the token/flag store that records whether the precondition is satisfied, because the agent could then mint its own permission.

A total-function session-lifecycle map found that only 80 of 83 reachable states in a live agent substrate could reach the clean successful-close terminal, because the close-out ritual is invoked explicitly by a skill with no hook arming it, so no automated guard fires when a session ends without running it.

A memory/reasoning substrate for LLM agents implemented a session-lifecycle guard architecture where five of six safety guards fail open (bypass on internal error, never block the operator's channel) and exactly one guard (a compiled block-action rule at the pre-tool-call stage) is fail-closed, by explicit design choice recorded in the codebase.

In one live agent substrate, an audit found 140 of 141 guard rules were unfenced by session-scope filtering, meaning a rule authored for one project's scope could fire in every other project's session; the fix added a tier gate (scope/global/portable) so a rule only fires where declared.

A stakes/ceremony-tiering law that is declared in project documentation and referenced by name in multiple memory records, but has no implementing classifier function, flag, or field anywhere in the executable codebase, represents the single largest gap between an agent substrate's declared laws and its running code.

Splitting a memory/knowledge-graph guard system into a compile-time phase (reads the persistent knowledge store, produces a compiled ruleset) and a fire-time phase (reads only the compiled ruleset, never queries the store directly) keeps the latency-sensitive per-action guard check fast enough for a blocking pre-action hook.

In one estate, documentation claimed a code module existed at a specific path under a renamed repository layout, but the path did not exist on disk; the actual, verified module lived elsewhere, illustrating that documentation claims about file locations can silently drift from the real code after a repo restructure.

A CLI verb in a live agent tool was wired into the command dispatcher but its target function used a zero-argument signature incompatible with the dispatcher's argument-passing convention, making the verb completely uninvokable (including for its own --help) despite being listed as available.

A raw grep over a codebase for direct database-mutation calls (cursor.execute/commit) was inconclusive for classifying which CLI verbs mutate persistent state, because most mutating code paths went through store helper functions rather than raw calls; the mutation classification had to instead rely on each verb's own declared help text and CLI grouping labels rather than a code-level write-path trace.

A source-string assertion that checks for a literal code snippet (e.g. via inspect.getsource) rather than driving the actual behavior will pass on a semantically broken rewrite that happens to keep the same string, and will break on a harmless reformat.

An UPDATE trigger that fires on column assignment rather than on value change journals a write even when no value actually changed, inflating write-count metrics without representing real state movement.

Splitting a database change-journal trigger into a narrow high-frequency 'tick' path (weight-only columns) and a full-payload path for structural columns can cut per-write journal size roughly tenfold while leaving read/recall performance unaffected.

A spec's headline measurement (e.g. database size, row counts) can go stale relative to the live system within weeks, so a design document's numeric justification should be re-measured before being cited again rather than trusted from the original spec.

A gate reviewer should re-run the original blind counter-test file unmodified before adapting it, because CT failures caused by harness-shape mismatches (auth walls, stub call conventions) are visually indistinguishable from real behavior defects until diagnosed one by one.

When a builder can read the same blind counter-test net the gate will use, green results on that net prove only that the letter of the tests was satisfied, not that the underlying behavior is correct; the gate must weight tiers the builder could not pre-read (interaction probes, sabotage) more heavily.
A gate should sabotage its own most-relied-upon check last, after all other verification tiers, to find whether that specific check would actually catch a regression in the property it certifies.
