A test that asserts a listener or field exists (presence) without asserting the effect it produces (e.g. that a UI badge actually clears on keystroke) can stay green while the entire behavior it was meant to guard is deleted.

A committed screenshot used as drift-gate evidence must be byte-reproducible from the same code and fixture; if regenerating it yields a different hash due to render-timing nondeterminism (e.g. a mid-fade toast), the render cannot itself serve as a gate.

Collapsing an external-call timeout into the same error path as a confirmed failure causes a system to treat an unknown-outcome write (e.g. a message that may have been delivered) as a definite failure, inviting operator retry and a duplicate side effect on the real target.

A dedupe/replay-protection window guarding a mutating action can be silently deleted while a full test suite remains 100% green if no test asserts the wire-level type (e.g. string vs number) or the presence of the guard's own call site, rather than just its parsed-dict effect.

A UI banner that names a broader promise than the code path can currently deliver (e.g. 'local data still shows' when the pane rendering that data is structurally unreachable from the current state) is a defect even when every individual guard is separately correct.

A test fixture that omits the exact API keys a code path depends on makes a correctness claim about that path untestable in the shipped harness, so a gate net can be 100% green while the claim it was meant to verify was never actually exercised.
A guard that fires after a dangerous action has already executed (e.g. after a send call rather than before it) provides no actual protection even if it is present somewhere in the code path.

A safety/kill guard that refuses an action silently (a bare early return with no recorded outcome) is functionally indistinguishable from a forgotten guard, because there is no audit trail proving the refusal happened at all.

A default parameter value on a dangerous action's function (e.g. dry_run defaulting to False on most but not all of several similar dispatch verbs) means that simply omitting the parameter at a call site becomes a live, irreversible action rather than a safe no-op -- inconsistent defaults across a family of similar functions are a live-fire hazard.

A count-only failure summary (incrementing a counter on exception) rather than per-item structured failure records makes individual failed operations unreviewable and unretryable, even though the aggregate failure count is technically visible.

Serving a filtered-empty result (e.g. an empty automation pool, an empty failure list) with no honest flag distinguishing 'the underlying operation found nothing' from 'the read itself failed' renders the empty state ambiguous and hides real outages as quiet success.

An automated pool-clearing action (removing every variant from a message template slice) that silences an automated flow should surface that consequence explicitly to the operator, rather than leaving the automation silently inert.

A read-only recon pass over a legacy codebase, restricted to file:line-cited claims with explicit unknown-markers for anything not directly verified, can produce a complete capability inventory (matching every item in a design spec to legacy code or an explicit gap) without touching or running the target system.

A folded compliance rule (e.g. 'AI-generated content must be visibly marked before send') that exists only in a verdict document citing a since-removed source document, with zero implementing code or marker field on the actual send payload, is unimplemented regardless of how many times it is cited as settled.

When a client-facing correctness rule (e.g. 'AI-drafted replies must be visibly marked') applies differently depending on the origin of the text (LLM-generated draft vs. owner-authored canned reply), marking only LLM-sourced content and not canned/template content avoids over-triggering a confirmation dialog on content that was never AI-generated.

Assembling an LLM prompt's context server-side from a re-fetched, trusted data source rather than trusting any client-supplied context field closes a prompt-injection surface where an attacker could smuggle arbitrary text into the model's context window via a normal API parameter.

Building an internal platform gateway as a stateless identity/contract layer that never becomes the system of record for business data (storing only append-only operational metadata) keeps the gateway's own failure modes decoupled from the business data's durability guarantees.

A scheduled read-only health probe of dependent services should report a dependency being down as data (a status payload) rather than raising a worker failure, so that a downstream outage does not crash the monitoring mechanism meant to observe it.

An append-only JSONL store using last-line-wins semantics for current state, with backward-tail reads and corrupt-line-skip-with-warning, is a viable pattern for a lightweight ingest journal that needs to be crash-tolerant without a full database.

When two independent writers can write to the same shared store (e.g. multiple machines writing directly to a bucket, plus a coordinating service also ingesting), the coordinating service's role becomes ambiguous -- it may be a lossy relay, a conflicting second writer, or an optional metadata journal -- and this must be explicitly decided rather than inherited from a prior single-writer design.

Running a data-extraction hook from inside the same session whose activity it is extracting can create a feedback loop, where the extraction process's own tool calls get recorded and re-extracted; a skip-while-syncing rule is needed to prevent this but is easy to omit from an initial design.

When a large numeric identifier (e.g. a 19-digit pagination cursor) crosses a JSON serialization boundary, it must be transported as a string rather than a number, because it can exceed the receiving language's safe-integer range and silently lose precision if parsed as a number.

A verbatim-ported constant (e.g. a dedupe window duration) that was correct in a prior page's context can silently drift from the intended value if it is copy-pasted rather than re-derived, so gate suites should explicitly pin such constants against the ruled value rather than assuming the port preserved it.

A build's own suite or test harness accidentally invoking a live external side-effect (e.g. reaching a real third-party API from a test path) constitutes a gate failure in its own right, independent of whether the code under test is otherwise correct.

In a tiered agent-delegation doctrine, escalating to a higher-capability model or a human is reserved for three specific conditions (a bounded drift/retry loop hitting a floor it cannot clear, a genuine fork between materially different directions where the cost of guessing wrong is high, or an irreversible outward act like a push/publish/payment), rather than for any planning decision that could be resolved from available context.

An orchestrator-tier agent role is defined by decomposing a goal into tier-tagged leaves and delegating strictly downward to cheaper tiers, verifying only the outcome of delegated work (via an on-disk acceptance check) rather than re-reviewing every line the delegate produced, on the reasoning that trust is earned because the delegate shares the same evidence substrate.

A strict-downward delegation rule (a task may only be delegated to a lower capability tier than its source, and the lowest tier has no further delegation target) is necessary to guarantee a delegation chain terminates; a delegation system without this constraint hit infinite recursion in its first real run.
A verification step that mutates its own index on a failing run is not idempotent: two runs on identical state report different findings.
Index rows from a verification scan must commit only on a sealed ok receipt; a failing run must leave every index file byte-identical.
A proposal re-checked after its own build is rejected for colliding with its own shipped symbols unless the checker has a post-build mode.
A duplicate-symbol scan at page-private granularity drowns in sibling-page idiom copies; declared page-private tiers must auto-acknowledge sibling dups while shared-library dups still error.
Resolving the memory room from the current working directory fails inside a build worktree; room-touching verbs need an explicit --room flag.
A spec-only blind counter-test seat, pinned to the base commit and forbidden from reading the builder's tree, finds spec-level defects that the spec author conceded before the build landed.
A contract fence whose selector keys on the wrong field fails open silently, degrading a hard freeze into an advisory.
Absence of a contract file should be advisory but presence-of-an-unloadable contract must be a distinct error, otherwise the fence cannot be told apart from a missing one.
A boolean fence on hand-written config must test identity (is True), not truthiness, because the string 'false' is truthy and would silently freeze the repository.
An empty scope-glob list that means 'applies to everything' is a freeze-all landmine; scope lists on a read-only fence must enforce minItems 1 and never route through the permissive matcher.

A clean gate report is a reason to look harder: fences that go quiet produce fewer findings, not more, so a build that reports 'all green, fewer errors than the pilot' is exhibiting the predicted symptom of suppression.
Idempotence must be asserted by byte identity of the index files, not by row count or set equality, because an upsert that rewrites keep+merged reorders rows while the set is unchanged.
Every idempotence or suppression test needs an anti-no-op twin, because an implementation that never writes (or acks everything) passes the primary test trivially.
A new verdict string not added to the CLI exit map silently inherits the reject exit code, so CI reads an 'amend' outcome as a hard failure.

When a proposal's budget is too small for the work, the honest move is to raise the declared budget with a stated reason; under-declaring touches to fit passes check and then surfaces as drift at bind.
Gate order should start with the single test on which every other test depends (e.g. 'does the contract even load'), then the two places where the build will look finished and be inert.
A machine-issued acknowledgement must be distinguishable in the receipt from a builder-issued one, or the receipt trail's honesty claim is unfalsifiable.
A post-pass that recomputes a field will overwrite an earlier-set value; a suppression flag set inside a step must be preserved by any later normalising loop.
Never pipe a test runner through head or tail for a gated claim; read the exit code.
Delegating downward is the default: every task goes to the cheapest tier that can do it, and a premium model is never spent on a mechanical write.
Escalation to a higher model is triggered only by a stalled drift-block, a genuine vision fork, or an irreversible outward act; planning decisions derivable from code or defaults are never escalated.
Drift escalates through a higher model before reaching the human, so a drift-block never dead-ends.
An orchestrator tier decomposes, tier-tags and delegates strictly downward, never hand-implements, and verifies the outcome by an on-disk acceptance check rather than by reviewing diffs.
An orchestrator that re-decomposes a leaf in place loops forever; splitting is done once at the top and lower tiers execute atoms without re-splitting.
A tier-seed atom is born neutral and only gains weight when a real orchestrated run composes a card that passes the on-disk DONE check.
Token pressure on a worker must never be what decides DONE.
The session lifecycle of the substrate can be modelled as a total-function graph and mechanically proven for totality and reachability: 20/20 checks over 83 expanded vertices and 259 edges.
Only 80 of 83 lifecycle vertices can reach the clean WRAPPED terminal because wrap is an explicitly invoked skill with no hook that arms it.
A guard is modelled as a push/pop frame around its caller rather than a static vertex, because its return address resolves at call time from the caller's contract.
All six lifecycle guards declare a fail-open bypass; exactly one disposition in the whole substrate is fail-closed.
The lifecycle graph contains zero vendor or model-name tokens, so it describes the organ the session runs inside rather than which model is plugged in.
A mechanical prover over a lifecycle graph proves the graph's internal consistency, not that the graph correctly describes the running code.
The stakes tier (SMALL/MEDIUM/LOAD-BEARING) had no classifier function, flag or field anywhere in the engine; it was held in model context only.
The weakest receipt grade on the primary session path is prose (self-attestation), and every such site must carry an explicit dark-organ marker.
A verb with a broken entry edge is modelled as not-a-node rather than silently included as if it worked.
A headless-browser screenshot of a standalone SVG file does not hit the ~485px viewport clamp that interactive pages hit, but this must be verified by checking output pixel dimensions.
A diagram renderer should assert at build time that every unique edge triple was drawn exactly once and raise rather than ship a mis-laid-out picture.
A first-pass verifier passed 10/10 on a graph in which an independent refuter then found 18 critical defects, because the proof covered static edge targets while guards resolved dynamically.
A second checker with a different blind spot is not optional; it is what caught the false-green proof.
Six successive grounding passes over a spec each deleted something that already existed in the estate, and each pass was cheaper than the last.
When a proven machine graph and its prose contract disagree, the prover runs only on the graph, so the losing side is rewritten to match the winner rather than both being kept.
Internal guard exhaustion routes to a suspended question and never parks directly; unattended runs degrade to PARKED only through a suspension TTL.
A contract that stops-and-asks too often becomes bureaucracy and gets bypassed, and a bypassed contract enforces nothing.
A workflow contract is a version, not an app: iteration is expected and the value is that a single-agent build does not leave the app half-finished on a blocker.
A worker brief that names the exact interpreter path prevents the shadowed-interpreter trap in a worktree that has no virtualenv.
The full test suite is run exactly once, pre-commit, with the real number reported verbatim; reassurance re-runs are banned because the gate re-runs everything.
A builder that finds a blueprint assumption false stops that step, writes a NEEDS-RULING entry, and continues other steps while the orchestrator rules mid-build.
The bare suite invocation from repo root is the suite convention; a subdirectory-only count is not the suite number.
Renders are committed with the code they certify and must be byte-reproducible.
A read-only recon worker marks every unverifiable claim as estimate (~) or unknown (-) and never asserts it, with file:line on every verified claim.
A blind counter-test seat reads only the pinned base commit via git show and never the builder's working tree or any later commit.
Counter-tests a seat cannot express are declared as INEXPRESSIBLE rows rather than faked, so the gate knows what the render probe must cover.
In a read-only installment every write-shaped assertion is a refusal assertion (the door must not exist yet); inventing mutation tests would be a false artifact.
A route rename against a seat's assumed path is a RETARGET, never a behaviour PASS, and a gate that reads a skip as green loses the floor.
A dedupe test suite self-poisons unless the in-process window is cleared between tests, because one test's identical send makes a neighbour's replay test falsely green.
A test harness must distinguish external timeout from external refusal as different exceptions, because a suite that cannot tell them apart cannot gate the UNKNOWN-vs-failed outcome.
A client-supplied context posted into an LLM draft route is a prompt-injection surface; the server must re-fetch the context itself.
Python's built-in hash() is unsafe as a cross-process dedupe key because PYTHONHASHSEED randomises it.
A 19-digit cursor transported as a JSON number silently loses precision past JavaScript's MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so it must be a string on the wire.

When the builder can read the blind seat's counter-test net, builder-green over those tests proves the letter not the spirit; the gate counterweights by running the original net unmodified and leaning on interaction-probe and sabotage tiers the builder could not pre-read.
Two-tier sabotage runs last: tier 1 guts a known guard and a test must go red; tier 2 sabotages the check the gate itself relied on most, and silence is a net-hole finding.
A gate verifies a build by evidence, never by the builder's testimony, and the gate must not have built it.
Committed render evidence that does not reproduce from the code at the gated commit is itself a finding.
At-rest render witnessing is insufficient; the gate must drive the interaction (click, force failure, follow links) and assert rendered values against fixture arithmetic.
When a mid-build ruling changes the spec, a blind seat test pinned to the pre-ruling reading is retargeted to the ruling, never to the builder's convenience.
A gate diffs the test file between base and build commit to catch any weakened or deleted prior-installment assertion that is not a declared supersession.
A direct service call that skips a live permission or gate check the board would have applied is a must-fix, so every declared deviation must be verified in code by the gate.
A builder-reported suite count of 1976 was unfalsifiable because it collected a subdirectory only; the gate measured 2485 at the same commit under the suite convention.
Deleting a guard while all 74 existing tests stayed green proved the net had a hole; the fix was a test on the raw response bytes rather than the parsed dict.
A heal brief fixes exactly the numbered must-fix items and nothing wider, and each fix ships with a red-on-gut proof stated verbatim for both runs.

A folded external timeout that is reported as a confirmed failure invites a double-send to a real recipient; timeouts must surface as UNKNOWN end-to-end with a plain retry deduped and an explicit resend bypass.
A presence-only test cannot see a deletion inside a handler; the pin must extract the handler body and assert the call lives inside it.
A parallel builder pass in the same worktree mid-build was reconciled by re-reading the rulings file and applying the missing ruling fixes before commit.
A builder names every deviation from the blueprint explicitly rather than hiding it, and declares deferred capabilities on-page with a reason rather than leaving them absent.
All twelve seat ambiguities were ruled before the write installment's builder report, leaving the builder with no unresolved assumption.
A blind seat found the real read seam the spec's degrade clause assumed absent, so shipping the degraded fallback would have been a failure to map an existing seam, not a legitimate degrade.
A round-2 gate verifies each heal claim against committed code and live runs, including a scope check that the diff touched only the heal-claimed files and no shared file.
The full suite grew 1897 → 2508 → 2514 across build, write installment and heal, each step reconciled by the exact count of added counter-tests.
Page-owned GET routes live in the shared main module by estate precedent, so a router-owned duplicate is removed at merge by the orchestrator, not the builder.
The blind seat's counter-test net is adopted into the page directory at merge so the test net ships with the page.
Journaling the full atom row on every weight tick made the sync journal 68% of a 465MB bank; 93,736 of 102,410 journal UPDATE rows were atom weight ticks.
A delta TICK trigger plus prune-on-ack yields about 20x tick speed and about 100x lower journal growth (24.2 to 0.23 MB/day) in a 26-day replay simulation, with recall speed unaffected.
A new trigger assertion must be proven to bite by temporarily re-fattening the trigger and watching the test fail before restoring it.
A burned runbook becomes a verb: journal pruning ships as a gc command that refuses when no peer acknowledgement exists.
A kill switch must record a skipped-kill row for every guarded door it blocks; a guard that refuses silently is a falsification target.
A dry-run evaluation must write zero run-log rows, falsified by counting rows before and after.
A server-side reconfirm guard must re-derive the recipient count and refuse with the fresh count when the client's expected count is stale; a client-only guard is a falsification.
A retry of a failed external send must reuse the original idempotency key on the wire; a fresh key is a duplicate send to a recipient.
The one legitimate live-send call site in a page tier must be reachable only through the reconfirm match and be structurally the only dry_run=False call site.
Empty template pools must surface a visible skipped-no-template honesty state on the card, never a silent zero.
Provider liveness must be defined as key-present AND a live call returned; a module that imports successfully with no key is a confident false positive, not a live tier.
On an estate where every paid model tier is dark, only the pure-Python $0 floor tier functions, so 'flow to the cheapest tier' becomes an availability discipline rather than a cost optimization.
Because every guard arming predicate runs at $0 on the code floor, the anti-drift guard layer stays operational on a fully keyless estate.

Uploaded documentation about a live system is not a source of truth for live state: reference docs claimed 25 built-in cartridges including a specific name, while the live registry reported 26 with that name absent.
A cartridge name in a workflow spec is valid only if it appears in the live registry; the validator must check every node's cartridge binding against the registry rather than trusting documentation.

Three successively cheaper grounding passes (bank index -> full atom bodies -> the running CLI) each caught defects the previous pass could not see; the gap between what a document claims and what the estate is closes only when something forces the check.

A workflow contract should bind competence (how to do a phase well) to earned cartridges and keep only the contract (that the phase happened, in order, with proof) in the graph; a node without a cartridge binding runs on model training instead of earned ground.

A revise node should route by failure class to a distinct fix discipline (unknown cause -> debug; wrong structure -> refactor; too slow -> optimize; too much -> slim) rather than binding one cartridge.

Hollow-receipt detection is the same mechanism as dead-claim detection on function names: an equipped honesty pass over the run's own receipts downgrades hollow receipts from structurally undetectable to detectable-when-a-tier-is-live.
A receipt must be bound to the run and node that produced it (run_id + node_id + content hash) or an artifact from an old run or a different node can satisfy a new node.
Any findings output must list the candidates considered and refused; a reframe without a rejected-candidates list gives no evidence the prior angles were evaluated.
A workflow graph should publish a T3-coverage metric (fraction of nodes completable with zero provider access) as an explicit build priority on a keyless estate.
The v1 model-tier vocabulary (reasoner / builder / taste / judge / council / local) was an invented tier ladder beside the estate's working OS/T1/T2/T3 ladder and was withdrawn in v2.
The v1 BLOCKED:DESIGN terminal was withdrawn in v2; an unanswered question is a suspension (SUSPENDED:QUESTION) on a warm channel that degrades to PARKED on TTL expiry, never a terminal.
v1 bounded nodes primarily by max_attempts; v2 withdrew that in favour of drift, TTL and budget bounds because a long productive polish pass is not a stuck run.

v1 modelled guards as first-class graph vertices with static edges; v2 withdrew this because a prover that validated static edge targets passed 10/10 while the runtime resolved guards through a bind field, so proofs must run over the expanded (guards-inlined) graph.

v1 applied one judge law (gate seat != producer seat) to every node; v2 split it: artifact gates need a seat distinct from every producer whose receipts they consume, while the finish-the-loop node must be self-judged because delegating lesson selection produces plausible unearned atoms.
v1's divergence guard was built on a two-band warm/cold bank temperature model while the live config defines three bands; the two-band assumption was withdrawn.

Viability ('real movement') must be defined as new validated receipts since the last check - never token count, turn count, message length or prose - so a stuck-loop guard cannot be satisfied by talking.

A per-node attempt counter must be written only by the nerve, incremented only on loop_back/on_fail entry, never reset within a run, and carried through park/resume so that resuming does not buy fresh attempts.

With a monotone attempt counter, a one-fire reframe latch, and no edge from the escalation decision back into the node, every path entering the viability guard reaches a terminal or a forward pass in at most max_attempts + 2 hops (5 hops at the default of 3).
A divergence guard that measures bank warmth must never use the witnessed fetch door, because fetching earns weight and the act of measuring temperature would raise it into self-confirmation.
Born-neutral atoms (never fetched, default score) must be excluded from a 'warm' count, otherwise a never-used atom presents as proven ground and falsely disarms the divergence guard.

Warmth thresholds (relevance floor 0.70, earned-score floor 100, minimum 2 hits) belong in editable config rather than code constants because bank density varies by scope age and consolidation passes re-score atoms under any fixed constant.

Guards must be evaluated in a strict precedence order - cheap-and-blocking first, expensive-and-speculative last - with only the first FIRED guard altering the route and the rest recorded as deferred, so evaluation does not depend on dict iteration order.
An unevaluable guard predicate must resolve to armed, not disarmed, and every disarm expires at the node boundary so a guard that disarmed on attempt k re-arms on attempt k+1.

Of five anti-drift guards, two cost nothing when armed and the three paid ones are bounded to one model call per node-attempt with a strictly cheaper disarm path, so the expensive branch is the exception.
An open-question record is valid only with text, owner, what-unblocks-it and what-was-tried all non-empty; a question without an owner is a complaint and the block edge cannot be taken.

A reframe guard that has fired once must report EXHAUSTED (not DISARMED) on its second arming and escalate, because conflating a spent bound with a benign skip lets an exhausted guard look healthy in the ledger.

A workflow receipt ledger must be append-only with each line hash-chained to the previous; a retraction is a new entry, never a deletion, because a mutable ledger reduces every downstream guarantee to 'the agent didn't lie'.

A state-transition function should be atomic-or-revert: snapshot, mutate, validate, contract-check, and restore original bytes on any gate failure - a pattern already proven in the estate by SHA256 identity before an invalid set and after revert.
Bound exhaustion (attempts, timebox, budget) is a legal transition to PARKED and must exit 0, not error, because every bound routes to a defined state rather than silence.

Three redundant enforcement surfaces (state nerve, agent engine narrowing, harness hooks) do not tamper-proof a workflow; their honest claim is only that every bypass requires a deliberate act and none can happen by a model forgetting or a context window rolling over.

A command-kind receipt is only as good as its declared command: a receipt whose proof command is `true` re-checks green and nothing mechanical catches it, so receipt commands must be human- or judge-readable in the ledger.

An escape hatch must be a logged nerve command, never an env var or hook toggle, because a toggle is invisible and permanent while a command is one countable append-only ledger line; repeated use (3 unplanted parks on one node) should arm the viability guard.
A session-start hook should print the outstanding exit receipts because that is the single fact a fresh context window cannot reconstruct and will otherwise confidently invent.

Lexical shell-escape detection in a pre-tool hook must warn rather than block, because shell analysis is unsound in both directions and a false block on Bash is the fastest way to get a hook disabled.
A harness hook should decide nothing it can ask the state nerve for: every conditional compares a nerve-computed field, so a change of law edits one Python module and leaves the JS untouched.

A bank-proposed autonomous goal must be reconciled against the flow token every turn (accept / reframe / reject-ahead / reject-behind / register), and the reconciler must never advance the token itself, so a loop that produces no receipts burns its bound visibly instead of inventing its next step.
A fresh relay worker's first action should be to read the flow state so it inherits position rather than re-deriving it from a summary - the anti-amnesia rule applied to workers instead of sessions.

A schema lock must be an artifact-hash receipt, not a file-exists receipt, because existence proves nothing about drift; the build node re-checks the stored hash against the live tree at entry so a stray write to the schema fails as an input gate rather than a build-time surprise.

A human decision gate must refuse to present its prompt until all input receipts are valid, no risk carries blocking severity without mitigation, and the success metric exists - the evidence gate runs before the human is asked, not after.

An automated override of a human-mandatory decision must force decided_by to a system value, require a waiver audit from a distinct seat, re-arm adversarial review, and tag the resulting atom as waived, so no 'go' is ever silently recorded as human.
Absence must be asserted, never implied: a risk or constraint receipt passes only with explicit entries or an explicit not-applicable flag with reasoning.

A feasibility spike gets exactly one attempt, a hard non-extendable timebox, and a write jail disjoint from the build jail, so spike code cannot become shipped code by construction and a timeout routes to a defined park rather than a retry.
A gate checklist is a refutation pass - any single failing row fails the gate - never a scoring average.
A continuous-gating verdict should be the nerve-computed AND of independent command exit codes, deliberately not an attestation, because there is no seat and no reasoning to attest.

All failure paths back into a producer node (its own check, the automated gate, the peer review) should consume one shared attempt counter, so the bound protects the producer rather than any individual gate.

Peer-review seats should rotate round-robin from a pool of at least three and reviewer reasoning should be dedup-checked across distinct artifact hashes, because a fixed reviewer pair satisfies the letter of 'not the producer' while enabling collusion or rubber-stamping.

v1 ran lint, unit tests and a security scan as a per-commit gate; v2 withdrew that because per-function microgates already prove conformance and the measured ~70% tool-wait share of wall-clock makes the full suite a once-per-ship gate on the seams between functions.

An observability receipt must be a live signal queried after the deploy timestamp (synthetic event round-tripped, logs from the new revision, a metric inside the post-deploy window); a config file proves intent while a live signal proves the pipe is open.

A deploy node may not pass unless the exact rollback command has been exercised (in staging or a canary slice) and its result re-verified before the rollout is accepted - rollback proof timestamp strictly precedes deploy timestamp.

A plant receipt must be proven by round-trip: the slug resolves through recall and fetches through the witnessed door after ingest; an ingest that exits 0 but whose slug does not resolve is a claim, not a plant.

The SHIPPED terminal must be reachable only through the finish-the-loop node, enforced by the terminal's receipt-set entry condition rather than node ordering, so even a miswired graph edge cannot ship without a plant receipt.

Memory atoms must be one lesson per file, self-contained (restating the bounded context rather than referencing the session), and use absolute dates so a cold recall hit months later reads correctly out of context.

Tier liveness should be probed once at boot and pinned for the run's TTL; later nodes read the pin rather than re-probing, so a tier flipping live mid-run does not retroactively unblock a parked node and a tier going dark does not silently downgrade a started step.

Stakes can be classified at $0 before any model runs from touched-path count, file-class globs, goal keywords, question-only shape, blast radius and an outward-facing flag; ties resolve upward because under-classifying ships a defect while over-classifying only costs ceremony, and SMALL means the graph does not run.

Where no earned cartridge exists for a task, the honest move is to bind a skill or connector and name the gap explicitly; evidence access is not competence (cartridge > skill > connector), and inventing a cartridge repeats the v1 fabrication defect.

A peer-review receipt should be external-grade (a platform PR approval by a login that is not the author, fetched live) so the judge law is platform-enforced; when the connector is dark the fallback to a recorded attestation must be logged and the run's status must report its weakest grade.
A design gate must treat the component atlas as the mandatory reuse anchor and fail any row where the design invents a component the atlas already holds an equivalent for.

A build phase is a loop of per-function microgates with its own bounds (2 polish loops per function, 180 s per function, debounce on hash stability), and the phase receipt is computed as every touched function having a passing receipt at its current body hash - never asserted.

Every failing gate must emit a failure_class (broken-unknown-why / structure-wrong / too-slow / too-much) that the revise node dispatches on; a missing or unrecognised class is a block, never a silent default to one fix discipline.

The last gate before delivery should run a receipt-honesty pass over the run's own ledger (dead-claim, silent-no-op, over-loaded, wrong-ID) and fail on any flagged row, so the run's evidence is audited before delivery believes anything the run claims.

A clean run through a well-worn path should plant nothing; plant one atom per distinct failure class actually hit, plant spike findings with their rejected candidates, and propose a reflex when the same trap shape recurs three times in a run.

Deciding which lessons a run learned must be judged by the run's own brain; delegating lesson selection to a different seat is borrowed self-recognition and produces plausible atoms that are indistinguishable from real ones until they mislead a future recall.

The live reflex ruleset is entirely act-guards: all 149 compiled rules fire on PreToolUse, 147 warn and 2 block, only 2 carry a conditional arming field, and zero rules cover omissions, because a match-on-command rule cannot see a thing that was never done.

Blocking guards should be reserved for irreversible writes to a source of truth and always carry a stated-reason override; the estate's ratio is 2 blocks in 149 rules (1.3%), and a guard that bricks the terminal is uninstalled within a day.

Conditional arming on cheap session counters (files written, workers dispatched) is the correct predicate style for guards and stakes tiering - $0, no model call - and a rule armed on every session is a rule someone eventually silences.

A blocking pre-tool hook that performs a cold Python import plus store load costs about 74 ms per call and compounds into a slowdown the operator feels; blocking hooks need a sub-10 ms budget via a persistent worker or memory-mapped read, with async used wherever the event allows.

Act-guards stored in a local reflex file do not sync to a cloud box while the bank and flow state ride the synced database, so a cloud-run agent has zero act-guard coverage but full omission-guard coverage.

A read-mirror of database state (kept so a blocking hook never opens sqlite) must carry the database sequence and tail hash and be asserted equal on validate, because two representations of one fact that can silently diverge is a green check with nothing behind it.

Pruning a ledger silently disarms any guard whose counter derives from it; the impulse to clean up substrate state is itself the drift signal, so any deletion or compaction of ledger/bank state must route through a decision node.

Internal drift exhaustion routes to a suspended question (owner call), not directly to PARKED; only external exhaustion (TTL, budget, dark tier with no fallback) parks, and an unattended loop's suspension TTL is zero so it degrades immediately to PARKED carrying the question, owner and receipts.

Restating the node contract in a transient per-step block that is rendered immediately before the model call and popped after is the mechanical answer to a model forgetting the basics, because a goal stated at turn 1 is forty turns behind by the time it matters and permanent reminders bloat the context trunk.

Permission mode must be config the loop itself owns, not an external sidecar auto-approver: a destructive-write interceptor that never saw the current mode fired on every overwrite regardless of mode, and the sidecar that had been built was retired as an anti-pattern.

A guard that cannot run (worker down, store locked, import error, timeout) must fail open and log a degraded entry, while a guard that ran and found a violation fails closed; a non-zero degraded count must weaken the run's reported grade, because a guard that fails open silently is absent.

The acceptance metric for re-enabling model keys is the fraction of a run's load-bearing decisions that carry a receipt a skeptical reviewer would accept without redoing the work - not graph proofs and not cheap-tier coverage, which optimises for permanent keylessness.

Never initialising the flow token disarms every conditional omission rule; the load-bearing catch is that the build door requires a valid token - you can work without a token but you cannot ship without one.

The ability to turn the whole enforcement contract off must be accepted as residual risk, because a contract that cannot be turned off gets routed around invisibly; a stakes tier that keeps ceremony off SMALL work is what makes the contract worth leaving on.

Before authoring a new enforcement law, check whether the estate already earned it as a dated reflex and promote that instead; four of the workflow's central laws already existed, one dated to a production incident.

A guard whose cited referents no longer resolve (a rule citing 91 atoms in a scope that holds 0) is worse than no guard because it is trusted; every guard must assert its referents still resolve and carry a fire/quiet test pair.

Shipping without a planted lesson earns a blocking guard under the estate's 2-in-149 block ratio, because the source of truth is the bank and the irreversible write is the one that fails to happen - the run's learning is destroyed when its context ends.

A build door with a valid-flow-token precondition is the single chokepoint where omission becomes detectable: you cannot ship what you skipped because you cannot build it, and the dependency is asymmetric so the substrate stands alone while the app cannot compile without it.
A blind counter-test seat that reads only the pinned base commit (never the builder's worktree or any post-pin commit) can catch spec ambiguities and defects the builder's own test net misses.

A PreToolUse safety hook can fail open on malformed or unsupported input (e.g. an unsupported schema version in its config), silently skipping enforcement instead of blocking the action, unless a specific severability guard requires exact single-line stdout with the diagnostic routed to stderr.

A generic mechanical-sweep review agent invoked with a bounded turn budget can stall (fail to complete) on a checklist item, requiring the orchestrating process to fall back to a single inline command per item instead of delegating.

A fenced approval process (a proposal gate binding declared file scope, introduced symbols, and referenced dependencies to the actual diff) closes the gaming path where a builder edits code outside its declared scope, but only if the binding step is verified against the diff rather than trusted from the proposal text.

A self-heal mechanism that re-scans a referenced file to resolve a symbol lookup can in principle be gamed by creating the file with the symbol just before the check runs, but a separate downstream diff-vs-introduces check can close that laundering path without adding complexity like mtime or hash comparisons.

A multi-lens automated review council (independent findings from separate perspective seats) can miss a real defect that a single dedicated skeptic pass catches by re-deriving the proposed fix against the existing design instead of accepting the council's diagnosis.

Two design documents in the same system can silently contradict each other on build order, and the deeper risk of the contradiction is not the doc mismatch itself but that a pilot build running in the wrong order will silently execute against an empty/unloaded contract set while reporting apparent gate completeness.

A machine-checkable convention registry (a contract) should not be created speculatively; it should be added only after repeated drift creates a measurable decision problem and at least one enforcing reader is ready to consume it.

A convention registry (contract) can be judged as earning its keep or being removed using measured criteria: rising reuse-resolution rate, falling duplicate-creation rate, false-positive gate rate under a fixed threshold, and zero unauthorized mutations to a read-only scope.

In a zero-semantic-duplication system, creation of a new symbol/utility should be gated behind a mandatory resolve step (reuse/extend/replace/create/reject) rather than allowed directly, because relying on an agent to remember to search first does not achieve zero duplication.

A workspace/session-state substrate (current project truth: cursor, working set, active change, blockers) should be architecturally separate from a long-term memory substrate (durable cross-project lessons), because the two answer different questions and the memory substrate is advisory unless explicitly promoted into current state.

A rendered visual defect (a scroll affordance drawn off the visible viewport) can be falsely confirmed as correct by the builder's own headless-browser screenshot, because a headless renderer can draw a UI chrome element (an overlay scrollbar) that the real device does not, masking the true layout offset.

Before adopting a sourced UI template, its authentication-flow assumptions (public signup, OAuth popups, multi-tenant switchers) must be audited and cut where they fight the product's actual auth model, rather than letting the template's structure dictate product decisions.

A citation/evidence audit that verifies source identity, line-range anchoring, and that the cited content actually supports the bounded claim (rather than merely existing) catches a distinct failure class from a documentation-completeness review.

When mining external tools/repos for ideas to adopt into an existing system, the correct discipline is to identify the delta the system does not already solve and adopt only that, rather than porting the external tool wholesale.

Marketing-derived claims about a tool being evaluated for adoption (star counts, 'fastest growing', token-volume claims) should be explicitly downgraded in credibility versus independently verified facts about the tool's real existence and architecture.
A budget cap on lines-of-code for a build deliverable can be enforced as a gate criterion, with overage flagged as a heal item even when the build is otherwise functionally correct.

A reclaim/onboarding catalog should be read in a fixed order (boot doc, ecosystem map, glossary/index, individual nodes, live progress board, session log) so a fresh session can orient without re-reading every source repository.

An agent operating over a large, partly-forgotten codebase has two characteristic failure modes: uncontrolled excitement-driven scope drift, and reimplementing functionality that already exists under another name; both are mitigated by writing findings down immediately and searching the existing system before building.

A documentation/reclaim node's status label should describe the catalog's current knowledge of a subject, not the subject's actual operational health, so a fully working component can still be marked as unmapped.
Diagrams generated from a typed, schema-validated JSON intermediate representation and compiled deterministically avoid the drift and rendering inconsistency of freehand SVG or Mermaid authoring.

A vendored third-party tool should be pinned to an explicit version by owner order, with update-checking scripts skipped entirely, so upgrades only happen via a deliberate re-vendor rather than silent drift.

A diagram-compiling pipeline should preserve the last-good rendered output on a failed build rather than overwrite it, and a non-zero validator exit code should never be treated as an acceptable partial result.

A large application scales past a threshold feature count only when engineers reason about one bounded package and its declared contract at a time, rather than the whole application, via four layers (door, host, wiring, package) each with a single, exclusive responsibility.
A software package is considered done only when its scenario suite passes against its declared interface and the assertions are mutation-tested, not merely when the code runs without error.

A configuration default that points at a specific developer machine path (e.g. a hardcoded drive path or an unset environment-variable fallback) is a defect: it must either fail loudly or resolve from shared estate configuration rather than silently working on only one machine.

Freezing a software package means recording its version, interface list, and a passing contract test in a manifest tag, not compiling it to a binary; binary compilation happens only at the final release/deploy step.

Five observable code smells reliably indicate a broken boundary-driven architecture: shared-venv coupling between repos (no host), tests scoped per file instead of per contract (no interface), previously-finished code getting re-edited (no freeze/reopen gate), a UI layer that also talks directly to the database (logic leaking into the door), and a project that cannot move to a new machine without a person's memory (wiring embedded in code/heads).

A structured engineering-delivery process built from ten discipline modules (product, UX, architecture, frontend, backend, data, QA, security, platform, analytics) sharing one procedural template still requires a separately loaded project-wide operating model (IMS) to answer project-wide readiness or requirements questions; the delivery skill alone cannot answer those.

In a multi-discipline delivery workflow, an actor that both builds and reviews the same artifact must disclose that the review is a self-review, since the review otherwise reads as independent verification it is not.

Under a specific baseline (IMS 1.1.0), a builder is structurally barred from gating or accepting their own candidate work; an independent pre-reveal counter-test and re-run/re-evaluation from another source is required before qualified verification can be claimed.

Loading or invoking a workflow/discipline skill module does not itself grant an agent permission to deploy, destroy data, spend money, publish, or start background/parallel agents; those require separate, actual host or user authorization.

An agent completing a delivery-discipline task must separate planned checks from executed results and report unperformed checks, blockers, assumptions, and residual risk explicitly rather than presenting a completed checklist as proof of quality.
Inspecting a specification document does not constitute execution of the underlying software, and this distinction should be recorded explicitly whenever a quality gate is evaluated.

A backend/API change is judged incomplete unless its verification exercises negative paths explicitly: invalid input, denied actors, cross-tenant or non-owner access, missing objects, duplicate requests, concurrent changes, and dependency failures.
Treating client-side checks as authorization is a named recurring backend-engineering failure pattern; authorization must be server-enforced.

Claiming production behavior from a unit test that uses mocked dependencies is a named recurring backend-engineering failure pattern; mocked and real integration results must be distinguished in reported evidence.
Generating a database migration script and marking it 'applied' without actually running it against an approved environment is a named recurring data-engineering failure pattern.
A destructive down-migration should not be treated as a complete data-recovery strategy, because it can reverse schema but not irreversible data loss.

Migration and data-model changes should be rehearsed against representative fixtures — including invalid and boundary data — in an approved non-production environment before being considered validated; a small fixture rehearsal does not prove production-scale performance.

A delivery coordination role should treat a completed-ticket count as insufficient evidence that a user-facing outcome actually works, and should not spin up every discipline module for a trivial change.

Roles within a delivery-coordination pipeline (Frontend, Backend, QA, etc.) are routing labels an agent can perform sequentially, not independent autonomous agents; calling them autonomous agents is a named failure pattern, and no background execution or inter-agent messaging should be claimed unless the host actually supports it.
A frontend implementation delivered only as a plan or an isolated code snippet, rather than an applied change in the actual repository, should not be reported as a completed implementation.
Suppressing errors or weakening a test in order to obtain a green test run is a named recurring frontend-engineering failure pattern that produces a false pass signal.
A prepared deployment checklist or runbook should not itself be reported as a completed release; release and recovery claims require actual execution evidence.

A code rollback should not be assumed to restore deleted data or reverse external side effects (e.g. sent notifications, third-party calls); platform recovery plans must treat code and data reversibility as separate concerns.

A before/after difference in product analytics data should not be presented as a proven causal effect; analytics recommendations must state sample limits, uncertainty, and causal assumptions rather than invented conclusions.
Missing analytics/instrumentation data should not be silently treated as zero usage, since absence of an event can reflect a tracking gap rather than absence of the behavior.

A product-management brief should not invent user interviews, quotes, usage volumes, or commercial impact figures; unsupported beliefs must be explicitly labeled as hypotheses rather than presented as evidence.

A multi-discipline engineering delivery skill enforces that observed evidence and unverified hypotheses must be recorded as explicitly separate fields, so a checklist alone can never stand in for a review result.

The delivery workflow requires every in-scope requirement to carry both an observable acceptance condition and a stated failure case, rejecting vague criteria such as 'intuitive', 'secure', or 'fast' without a measurable condition.

The Product Management discipline forbids treating the author/builder as the default acceptance authority; acceptance must be evidenced by the real, separately identified authority or explicitly marked pending.

An outcome metric definition is incomplete unless it states population, numerator, denominator, observation window, data source, and baseline status; feature completion or raw event volume alone is disallowed as proof of user value.

A QA/quality-engineering process treats a completed test plan as a produced artifact only, never as evidence the application actually passed, and forbids rerunning a flaky test until green without investigating the instability.
A QA discipline requires disclosure whenever the same actor both built and verified an artifact, since a self-review cannot be represented as independent review.
Test check status must be recorded from a fixed enumeration (planned, passed, failed, blocked, not_applicable, unknown) and 'unknown' is explicitly disallowed from counting as a pass.

A security-engineering discipline requires that a dependency/vulnerability scanner finding be confirmed by actual version, reachability, and configuration before it can be treated as demonstrated exploitability, and forbids treating a clean scan as proof no important threats remain.

Active security testing is scoped so that read-only design/code review can proceed on supplied materials alone, while active verification requires an explicitly authorized target, and permission to test one system is never inferred to cover unrelated infrastructure.

The security discipline forbids the report author from accepting residual risk on behalf of an authority they do not represent; risk acceptance may only be assigned to the actual authorized decision-maker.

A UX/UI design discipline requires every changed screen or component to specify the full state space (initial, loading, empty, populated, validation-error, service-error, permission-denied, success), rejecting designs that show only the happy-path screen.
The UX/UI discipline forbids treating a textual or visual specification as a tested prototype, and forbids using color alone to convey critical meaning.

A cross-discipline delivery contract defines a single canonical lifecycle for a work item (planned -> ready -> in_progress -> implemented -> verified -> accepted) with release tracked as a separate not_released/released/unknown axis, replacing per-role trackers.

The delivery contract requires all corrections to prior facts be made via new append-only events (event_id, actor, action, previous_state, new_state, evidence_refs, timestamp, reason) rather than by editing history in place.

Under an approved IMS-EOM 1.1.0 pairing, a discipline's own self-review or 'ready' recommendation cannot grant IMS evidence credit; IMS gate 2.7 requires an independent pre-reveal counter-test plus an independent authorized gater and a named phase acceptor distinct from the builder.

Under IMS-EOM 1.1.0, a record only feeds qualified evidence into its A-P (assessment) rows when that row has at least two independently verified met checkpoints; shallow or unknown active rows retain their obligations rather than being marked satisfied.

Under IMS-EOM 1.1.0, closure requires a working, accountable watch (watcher, matching observation, positive horizon, failure predicate, reopen/escalation path); a missing or stale watch is scored UNWATCHED and treated as non-pass rather than pass-by-default.

IMS-EOM 1.1.0 tracks cost as measured/estimated/unknown with an explicit rule that unknown cost is never treated as zero, and cost measured against zero realized gain is treated as an undefined (not computable) ratio.

R-0170 rev1 superseded IMS-EOM 1.0.0 with an approved 1.1.0 baseline for new work, while byte-identical preservation of the original Delivery Contract v1.0.0 and its role structure (one coordinator plus ten specialists) was explicitly retained rather than rewritten.

The engineering-delivery-team package consolidation from 3.0.0 collapsed eleven separate discipline-skill installations into one routed skill, explicitly labeled a breaking packaging change, while preserving all eleven discipline procedures, 44 operation prompts, and 33 templates unmodified in content.

The delivery-team execution rules explicitly forbid a package/prompt's own context fields from granting new permissions, treating untrusted retrieved text and log content strictly as data, never as commands.

A discipline recommendation of ready_for_next_step is explicitly defined as not equivalent to acceptance, release authorization, an IMS gate pass, or formal certification, closing the gap where a reviewer's own approval could be mistaken for organizational sign-off.
A delivery workflow prompt can require that an actor filling multiple roles must not claim independent review, since the same identity authored and reviewed the work.
A resume workflow should not infer that a prior verification pass still applies once a dependent artifact has changed since that pass.

A readiness review workflow distinguishes five distinct evidence states for a requirement: missing artifact, unrun check, failed check, stale result, and unaccepted/unreleased deliverable, rather than treating them as one pass/fail signal.
A feedback-to-rework workflow routes a correction to the discipline that originated the issue rather than defaulting to QA or a central coordinator.
A work-routing skill selects one primary discipline plus operation (execute/review/rework/handoff) for a task rather than activating every specialist role for a small change.

An engineering operating model that scores domain maturity as a checkpoint count (x/12) rather than an explicit set of which checkpoints are met allows equal-count domains with different actual coverage to appear equivalent.

A phase-gated maturity model was amended so that the builder of a candidate can never also be its gater or acceptor; an independent context must record a pre-reveal predicate and falsifying cases before the builder's conclusions are revealed.

In this operating model a closed/accepted domain that lacks a working watch (accountable watcher, positive staleness horizon, and a recent successful observation) must be displayed as 'closed, UNWATCHED' and treated as non-passing, rather than remaining a silently green closed row.

A local command success, mock reply, or queued request does not prove an intended external-system mutation occurred; only a target-side observation matched by operation/idempotency key and intended state counts as evidence of external effect.

An engineering operating model can require full domain records (A-P) only for active domains with at least two independently verified met checkpoints, so deferred/inapplicable domains keep a lighter record (reason, consequences, owner, trigger) without full ceremony.

An AI model/provider used as a dependency should be admitted through the same risk-based dependency-admission process as any other dependency, requiring independent live evidence of its actual decisions rather than a routing test alone.

A locked engineering baseline allows a later technical decision to specialize a rule but not silently contradict it; any contradiction must be surfaced as an explicit amendment proposal rather than quietly overridden.
A phase-gated completion model treats one broken correctness/security-critical (S-class) domain as a hard blocker that cannot be averaged away by high scores in other domains.

A leverage-discipline default engineering reaction ranks native code as the last option: eliminate, configure, reuse, adopt a standard, adopt open source, use a managed service, wrap, extend, fork, then build from scratch.

A build discipline recommends concrete-before-generic: implement one real path, then a second, and generalize only once repeated structure is actually observed, instead of predicting future uses and generalizing immediately.

An engineering operating model separates 'Experimental' as a parallel capability state usable alongside a Stable core, not a chronological phase after Beta, so an experimental capability cannot weaken the Stable core's invariants.
A dependency-admission gate scales review depth to blast radius via five risk classes (D trivial to S correctness-critical), rather than applying uniform scrutiny to every dependency.

An amendment to a locked engineering baseline (IMS-EOM 1.0.0 to 1.1.0) was approved by moderator judgment under explicit owner delegation rather than by the owner's own signature, and the record explicitly distinguishes that delegated authority from direct owner approval.

A migration plan for adopting a new evidence-schema version explicitly refused to convert a legacy scalar maturity score (e.g. '3/12') into an inferred set of specific checkpoints (e.g. {1,2,3}), because a count does not establish which checkpoints were actually met.

A validation run for a two-version documentation package passed 22 of 22 static checks, and the one failure in the first pass was a checker bug (comparing a qualified alias against an unqualified ID) rather than a defect in the source documents.

A drafting unit explicitly distinguished 'structurally valid' (passes a JSON-schema check) from 'qualifies as proof', stating that a structurally valid but field-unknown evidence record earns no credit.

A skeptic-corrected engineering model records that an evidence-depth score (x/12) is normative as a shorthand for a set of proven checkpoints, not a percentage, and that creating documents does not by itself earn maturity credit.

A command-center IMS domain-tracking assessment applying the operating model to itself found most domains stuck at Planning-level depth (3-5 of 12 checkpoints) with every checkpoint gate result recorded as 'Uncertain' rather than pass, because no owner was assigned and no independent verification had run.

A self-applied IMS assessment found the security/authorization domain's checkpoint 3 (assumptions) specifically uncredited because a source auth flag failing-open exposure was unverified, and treated this as a hard-gate finding rather than a normal depth gap.

A test-result correction record found that four failing tests attributed to a product defect were actually caused by a missing executable shim not on the interpreter's PATH, and explicitly classified this as an environment gap rather than an unresolved defect or a pass/waiver.

A test-result correction record found that two extra test failures in one run were caused by an inherited environment variable (a seat-role contamination) rather than a product defect, and explicitly excluded them from the product suite's pass/fail count.

An evidence register explicitly separated 'a document describing a check exists' from 'the check ran', flagging that no fresh test run, no live-box evidence, and no external-effect reconciliation were claimed by the extraction itself.

Copying a live SQLite database file in WAL mode with a plain file-copy (cp/copy2) can save a stub file with no tables, so a safe backup of a live WAL-mode bank requires SQLite's online-backup API rather than a raw file copy.

A file copied with shutil.copy2 preserves the source file's modification time, so a backup's mtime reflects when the source was last written, not when the backup snapshot was actually taken, which can make a stale backup look fresh.

A domain-tracking register that inventoried a project's full domain scope against a canonical 77-domain model found most domains fell into three roughly equal buckets: about 39% active, 31% inapplicable, and 30% recognized-but-deferred, rather than the majority being active.

A single-shot multi-model bake-off using a fixed rubric (truth, code-reasoning, format-compliance, justification) across models at different price tiers can rank them for role-specific routing (e.g. audit vs draft vs bulk-transform) rather than picking one model for every task.

In a bake-off of LLMs on a factual API-existence probe, larger/flagship-tier models correctly refused to answer a nonexistent API property while smaller/cheaper-tier models confidently hallucinated a specific wrong answer with no hedging.

A model that leaks its intermediate reasoning/thinking trace before a final answer can still be useful for fact-checking because a caller can detect uncertainty in the leaked trace even when the final stated answer is wrong or overconfident.

Routing an audit/verify pipeline through two independently-sourced reasoning models (one paid, one free/different-vendor) for audit and cross-check respectively produces a second opinion that will not simply rubber-stamp the first model's findings.
A cross-repo shared interface (a contracts/schema surface) should be versioned as its own scope so that changing it is treated as a cross-repo event, never silently broken.

A memory substrate atom is a weight-adjustor that reshapes a model's understanding on read, not merely a stored record, which is why one lesson per file (an atom) works but dense multi-lesson files do not.
Recall functions as foveated vision: querying by current intent brings matching atoms into sharp focus while unrelated atoms remain dormant but retrievable, rather than surfacing everything at once.
An atom's significance (weight) must be earned by trace evidence that a procedure using it succeeded, never self-asserted by the atom or the model that wrote it.

A recall verdict of warm versus cold should function as the routing signal for whether an agent re-treads a proven procedure (reflex) or generates a fresh approach and later crystallizes it as a new atom (think).

Automated deploy/config state-change tooling that always runs its full validation discipline (mutate, regenerate derived docs, run two independent validators) prevents documentation/topology drift that occurs when the same steps are done manually and get skipped.

In a memory substrate, cartridges are swappable earned capability cores (mapped as atom=parameter, card=transformer, warmth=attention, trace=training) that let an agent load a proven capability by name instead of re-deriving it from scratch.

A UI-building agent should emit a small schema-bound typed tree of nodes rather than one large HTML blob, so that generation lands as reviewable diffs and avoids the failure mode where a model stalls trying to edit one giant file.

A web dashboard that reports live agent/runner state should render an honest 'idle'/empty state with an explanatory note rather than fabricate activity when the backing process registry is not reachable from that layer.
A web application layer should import only a single designated services gate module rather than reaching into internal modules directly, so an architecture scanner can enforce the boundary.

Persistent multi-agent (society) builds that use a background streaming session must pre-set the allowed tool list at launch, because a permission gate mid-session can stall an unattended peer forever.
A persistent multi-agent watcher must advance its message-bus read cursor to the current tip once on launch, otherwise a stale control message sent to a prior peer can kill a freshly started peer.

A read-only, non-destructive peek into an inter-agent message bus should use a separate cursor table from the consuming worker's cursor, so a human inspecting traffic never advances the state a live agent relies on.

When an orchestrator gates work built by a delegated agent, it should re-run the test suite itself, read the diff, and run a live smoke test independently rather than trust the builder's own report of success.

A one-shot task-graph executor (board) and a persistent gated multi-peer executor (society) are complementary, not interchangeable: the task-graph planner should be reused only to DRAW the work plan, while a persistent watcher executes it, because one-shot nodes cannot carry context across rounds the way a persistent peer can.

A frontend SPA that supports two operating modes/surfaces should run a boot-time assertion verifying every declared route has both a DOM page container and a loader entry, to catch broken route wiring before a user hits it.

Native HTML select-element interactions are not reliably driven by simulated DOM input/click events because the framework's change-event handler does not fire; only a CDP-level value-set plus explicit dispatchEvent('change') reliably triggers dependent UI cascades.

Browser automation object handles (CDP objectId) do not survive across separate protocol calls; a stable node-based lookup path (querySelector by nodeId) is required for operations like file-input uploads that need a persistent handle.

Reading a live rendered DOM as structured text is sufficient as the primary sensing channel for driving a real web app end-to-end; pixel/screenshot capture was never needed as more than a tiebreaker in a full multi-step funnel drive.

An invite-only web service should validate role gating server-side on every authenticated API route rather than trust client-side hiding, and never expose a public signup route if the product is meant to be admin-provisioned only.

A web service backed by a shared memory substrate should read the substrate in-process rather than shell out to its CLI, so that user-supplied browser input only ever fills a parameter and never becomes an executable verb/argv.

Frontend engineering discipline should be organized as always-on cross-cutting laws (naming, single-responsibility, single-source-of-truth state, DOM/layout isolation, defensive boundaries) plus a gated phase sequence (contract translation, brand shell, data hooks, atomic UI wiring, aesthetic hardening), where each phase gate must pass before the next phase starts.

Frontend API types should always be generated from the backend's OpenAPI contract rather than hand-written, so that renaming a schema property breaks the build at compile time instead of failing silently at runtime.

A frontend feature's business logic and async state machine should be built and proven functional against an unstyled HTML page before any visual styling is applied, so that later bugs are cosmetic rather than logical.

UI state should minimize stored values by deriving computable fields at render time and by collapsing combinations of independent boolean flags into a single explicit status enum, because independent booleans can represent impossible/contradictory states.

A composable multi-phase capability pipeline can bind a specialized discipline cartridge into a specific phase of a broader pipeline (e.g. slotting a frontend-engineering discipline between a design phase and a QA/proving phase) purely by recording the binding as a memory atom, without editing the orchestrator's built-in configuration.

When a persistent bug investigation stalls after two plausible-but-wrong hypotheses, the fix is to stop reasoning and go read raw ground-truth evidence (logs, wire dumps, actual file bytes) rather than generate a third theory.
Any invariant that must always hold (id uniqueness, edge reciprocity, size caps, path jails) should be enforced by code, never left as an instruction a model is merely expected to follow.

A work session is not complete when a fix works; it is complete only when the lesson is written as an atom, ingested into the bank, indexed, and the receipt committed, otherwise the memory substrate never actually learns from that session.

A memory substrate atom's weight can only be lowered by the reader who was actually misled by it (a fire_lower path), and weight decays rather than deletes; there is deliberately no symmetric fire_higher path because weight can only rise through witnessed use, not self-assertion.

An architecture-enforcement static scanner that runs at import time and blocks upward imports (lower layers importing higher layers) and private-module bypasses turns architectural rules into a hard ImportError boot gate rather than a lint warning that can be ignored.

In a session-boot ceremony for an LLM agent, the majority of the fixed boot-context cost is restated documentation/prose that already lives in the queryable memory bank and can be cut without losing capability, since recall-on-demand covers the same ground.

A body-preservation test that asserts the freely-editable machine-generated header of a memory index file can be swapped (full vs. lean variant) while the user-authored content below a delimiter stays byte-for-byte identical is a reliable technique for shrinking boot cost without risking data loss.

When multiple capability modules in a registry share similar names/descriptions, the apparent overlap is often namespace sprawl in labeling rather than actual duplicated payload content, and this should be verified by reading the underlying files, not by comparing names/descriptions alone.

A memory-scoring system that recomputes an atom's decayed score at read time (rather than storing a pre-decayed value) lets old positive contributions fade gradually while very recent contributions show near-zero decay, and lets different atom types decay at different rates (e.g. feedback atoms decay slower than reference atoms).

A memory bank can implement view-through decay by logging which atoms were shown (impressions) versus which were actually opened, then demoting atoms that repeatedly lose competing impressions without ever being opened, capped and floored so decay never erases an atom entirely.

A full-fidelity bank export/import (portable document with manifest, per-table schema introspection, and typed coercion) is a different capability from a binary file-copy backup: the export survives schema drift between engine versions and can merge into a live bank, which a raw file-copy backup cannot.

A bank-import routine that creates a fresh destination database must initialize it through the exact same canonical schema-migration code path the live engine uses to open a database, otherwise migration-added columns silently vanish on round-trip even though the round-trip equality test passes.

Cycle-detection logic designed to guard a live write path must not be applied to a document-restore/import path, because a tombstoned supersession edge (a merge receipt recording that two atoms were once merged) is essential evidence for future merge-conflict handling and must survive a restore verbatim, even if it forms part of a graph cycle.

Claims that a persistent memory substrate improves agent performance should be pre-registered as falsifiable, dated predictions with named metrics and pass/fail thresholds before the evaluation window, because self-attested claims of value are otherwise unfalsifiable.

A reflex/guard-rule fire log should be evaluated for precision (true-positive fires over total fires), because a low-precision alarm channel trains the human/agent operator to ignore it, which silently defeats the whole point of banking a guarded trap.

A porting/ingestion pipeline should discard the source material's structural wrapper (its tool-specific fan-out format) while retaining only the domain knowledge content, when the target system already has its own equivalent orchestration mechanism.

A newly registered capability module (cartridge) that references atoms not yet ingested into the bank should visibly report a fractional resolution count (e.g. 0/9 resolved) rather than silently appear complete, so operators can see the ingest step is still required.

A cross-cutting doctrine discovered while porting a narrow domain corpus (e.g. requiring every findings/opportunities output to include a section of explicitly rejected candidates) can be general operating law for the whole system even though it lives inside one narrow capability module.

Publishing part of a private codebase to a new public repository should be done via a fresh repository built from an allowlist-based export (never by copying/pushing the existing history), so that any secret ever committed to the private repo's history physically cannot travel to the public copy.

An export tool that copies files into a public-release directory should use an explicit allowlist of paths rather than a blacklist, because a blacklist can silently miss an unknown or newly added file that should have been excluded.

A secret-leakage scanner gating a public export should target the specific shape of secret material (e.g. private-key hex patterns, files under a known secrets directory) rather than naively flagging any file with a suggestive name, to avoid false positives on unrelated files that happen to share a filename.

Documentation drift (stale verb/module/cartridge counts) should be fixed by a deterministic script that parses the live CLI help output as the single source of truth, rather than by hand-editing counts in multiple docs, so future drift is caught by re-running the generator instead of manual audits.

A CLI's onboarding flow for a first-time user should close the full loop (install to first successful query) in one command by seeding demo content, ingesting it, and running a sample query automatically, rather than requiring the user to author their own first data before seeing the tool work.

A query against an empty database should never return a bare 'no results' response indistinguishable from a bug; it should explicitly state the database is empty and name the exact command to populate it.

A chat/conversation service should bound its prompt history by a fixed token budget applied BEFORE any provider call, dropping only whole turns (never partial ones) from the oldest end, and should report how many turns were dropped rather than silently truncating.

A login rate limiter should check the lockout state BEFORE verifying credentials, and its locked-out response should be identical in shape whether or not the account exists, so the rate-limit response itself cannot be used to enumerate valid accounts.

A reverse-proxy client-IP header (X-Forwarded-For) should only be trusted when the connection originates from the known proxy's own address (e.g. localhost); otherwise an external attacker can forge the header to evade per-IP rate limiting.

A memory substrate's atom read path can distinguish a free 'peek' (spine/metadata only, no scoring effect) from a paid 'fetch' (full body, earns weight) so that browsing costs nothing but consuming a lesson strengthens it.

New memory atoms should be created with a neutral born score rather than an asserted high or low confidence, so that an atom's rank is earned entirely through subsequent witnessed use rather than self-report at creation time.

Session-boot ceremony text (banner + summoning + per-turn seed) that restates content already retrievable on demand from the memory bank can be compressed by roughly 40-50% without losing load-bearing law content, by keeping only doctrine/laws/entry-verbs verbatim and replacing per-atom listings with counts or top-N samples.
